items.how: Map a city name to a tz offset (static table of major cities, or a free geocode/timezone API via fetch_json), or ask one follow-up "what timezone?" when a city is captured without one.

items.title: no paywall/login-wall detection when summarizing an article
items.why: Pasting an NYT/WSJ/Medium link + "summarize" returns the paywall stub summarized as if the article, or a generic error.
items.how: Detect paywall/metered markers in the scraped page (or a near-empty body on a known-paywalled host) + a friendlyError "paywalled" category that offers the free bits/another source.

items.title: background errand lost on restart (spoken promise broken)
items.why: "On it — I will text you when done" then a deploy/crash mid-run: the result never arrives, no error, no resume. In-memory only, unlike schedules/alerts.
items.how: Persist pending background errands to a JSON store; on startup re-dispatch (or notify) any that were in flight.

items.title: watch -> then run a recipe (active watch-and-do)
items.why: Alerts only ping; the non-gated slice of Instinct continuous-acting is: when a watch fires, auto-run a follow-up READ recipe and send its result.
items.how: Add a "then <recipe>" field to an alert; alert-runner runs the recipe on fire + sends its output. Stays read-only.

items.title: watches keep only lastValue — no trend/history
items.why: "how has X moved this week" impossible; alerts forget the past.
items.how: Append value+timestamp per check to a capped series; answer trend/min-max/since-date from stored data, no LLM.

items.title: crash-recovery replay: data-loss gap, poison loop, double-ACK
items.why: Audit of the just-shipped background-errand-persist found 3 defects: drain-then-async-reinject lost errands if recovery itself crashed; a poison errand re-injected through handle reset startedAt + had no attempt cap, so it crash-looped + re-spammed every boot; and replay double-messaged (recovery notice + a fresh ACK).
items.how: Shared dispatchBackground closure + handle.resumeErrand run a replay under its EXISTING id (no new record, no ACK); store no longer drains (list+reinstate bumps attempts in place); planErrandReplay drops a poison errand after MAX_ERRAND_ATTEMPTS.

items.title: web_search single-provider (Bing scrape) no fallback
items.why: The headline "ask anything" path scrapes only bing.com/search; a bot-check or markup change makes a new user first errand return nothing, no DuckDuckGo/Brave fallback.
items.how: Add a keyless fallback engine (DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint) behind the same webSearch interface; try Bing then fall back on empty/error.

items.title: live FX / currency conversion via a JSON endpoint
items.why: "200 USD in EUR right now" improvises a slow web_search+scrape that is often stale/mis-parsed; should be instant.
items.how: Wire a keyless exchange-rate JSON API via fetch_json (same class as the open-meteo weather path); prompt/tool hint to use it for FX.

items.title: Telegram location-pin messages silently dropped
items.why: Tapping attach->Location (the natural "near me" move) sends a text-less message that is dropped with no reply — reads as broken.
items.how: Parse msg.location.{latitude,longitude} in the telegram intake; feed coords to the agent (enables precise near-me) or at least acknowledge + offer to save as location.

items.title: once reminder can be starved indefinitely behind the hourly cap
items.why: An over-cap "once" reminder is deferred with no age/attempt limit while recurring tasks eat the slots — an explicit promise (meds at 3pm) can slip indefinitely.
items.how: Age-out: once a deferred once-reminder is overdue by > N, fire it regardless of cap (or notify it could not be delivered on time).

items.title: CSV/table export of compare & extract results
items.why: A multi-item compare returns a JSON array truncated in chat; a keepable CSV is far more useful + reusable.
items.how: Format the compare/extract JSON array -> CSV, send via the existing sendDocument path (only pdf uses it today). Pure formatter, offline-testable.

items.title: watchlists — N items, one grouped ping
items.why: A user with a basket (5 stocks / 3 job feeds) must define N separate alerts + get N pings; a watchlist groups them into one standing dashboard.
items.how: A member array on an alert + a combined formatter reusing the alert store; ping only the moved items in one message.

items.title: watchlist member fan-out unbounded + CSV formula injection
items.why: Audit found the just-shipped watchlist ran Promise.all over up to 8 members, bypassing the DISPATCH_CONCURRENCY pool bound (reintroduces browser-pool exhaustion; degraded members silently dropped from the ping). And CSV export did not guard formula injection from scraped cells.
items.how: mapPool at WATCHLIST_CONCURRENCY (default 3) for member checks; csvCell prefixes =/+/-/@ cells with a quote.

items.title: weather/near-me/directions have no backend (LLM-guessed API)
items.why: The #1 first errand "weather" + the advertised "near me"/"directions"/"how far" all lack a real tool — the agent guesses a forecast URL or scrapes a JS map shell and floods/fails. LOCATION_ERRAND_RE + saved coords already exist; only the backend is missing.
items.how: A keyless geo cluster over Open-Meteo (geocode + forecast), Nominatim (place->coords), OSRM (route distance/ETA), Overpass (nearby POIs). Start with weather (highest frequency) as get_weather via fetch_json + a geocode step; honor profile coords/units.

items.title: shared coords leak to the LLM forever with no TTL
items.why: A location pin shared once keeps sending ~1m coords to the external LLM on EVERY later message (incl unrelated ones) + "near me" resolves against a stale spot; static pins are stored permanently.
items.how: Expire pin coords after a TTL (e.g. a few hours) so they inform near-term near-me but do not persist as "current"; drop them from contextLine once stale; keep the free-text home location durable.

items.title: convert_currency claims "live" but rate is ~daily + tiny rates render 0.0000
items.why: The FX source refreshes ~daily; the tool tells the user "the rate is live" (misrepresentation for a money decision) and a small inverse rate shows "rate 0.0000".
items.how: Surface the API time_last_update_utc + drop the "live" wording (say "as of <date>"); format the rate with adaptive precision so a <0.01 rate is not 0.0000.

items.title: draft-to-send composer (non-gated acting slice)
items.why: Relay is read-only + dead-ends at "here is what I found"; the honest non-gated answer to Instinct acting is composing the email/DM/reply as a ready artifact the USER sends.
items.how: A compose intent -> LLM drafts the message + a copy block + a mailto:/tel: deep link; never hits send (safety guard untouched).

items.title: watchlist member labels can collide
items.why: memberLabel = first 4 words; two similar members collapse to one label so setMemberLasts updates the wrong one + one member re-fires every check.
items.how: Disambiguate duplicate labels (append an index) or key members by task, not label.

items.title: CSV formula-guard corrupts legitimate negative numbers
items.why: The just-added CSV injection guard quoted any cell starting with - (a negative price/temp/%-delta) as text, so the exported sheet could not sort/sum that column — broke the deliverable it exists for.
items.how: Skip the quote for a plain numeric cell (-?d...); still guard a non-numeric =/+/-/@ lead.

items.title: "near me" / local place search has no backend (advertised, broken)
items.why: Onboarding + the location-pin ack promise "near me"; LOCATION_ERRAND_RE detects nearby/closest but there is no POI tool, so the first location errand flounders on a logged-out map scrape.
items.how: Nominatim geocode + Overpass around:<coords> query by category -> name/distance/opening_hours/phone; keyless. Reuse the weather fetchText pattern.

items.title: directions / travel-time promised but unbuilt
items.why: "how far is the airport", "directions to X" match LOCATION_ERRAND_RE + are advertised, but no routing tool exists — returns nothing usable.
items.how: Nominatim geocode both endpoints + OSRM public server (router.project-osrm.org, keyless) for distance+duration; one-line ETA reply.

items.title: get_weather resolves an ambiguous city to the biggest same-name match
items.why: "weather in Portland/Springfield" returns the highest-population match, not the user; count=1 + results[0] with no disambiguation.
items.how: Fetch a few geocode candidates; if the top two are far apart / different regions, ask which, or prefer one near the user saved coords.

items.title: .ics calendar export in the composer
items.why: A found event/deadline dead-ends at text; no add-to-calendar. compose.ts already proves the non-gated artifact pattern.
items.how: compose kind:calendar -> a data:text/calendar VEVENT + a Google-cal deep link; pure formatting, never trips the send guard.

items.title: recipes give the single arg to EVERY slot
items.why: applySlots stuffs one arg into all slots (its own comment flags it), so "track {item} at {store}" cannot take two values — recipes stay toys.
items.how: Parse distinct positional/named args; map each to its slot.

items.title: compose echoes an invalid recipient but blanks the deep link
items.why: A malformed to shows "To: john at x.com" in the copy block yet the mailto/sms link has an empty address — tapping opens a blank draft; user thinks it is addressed.
items.how: When to fails EMAIL_RE/PHONE_RE, omit the To: line + note the address could not be parsed, or keep it out of both.

items.title: calendar_event crashes the turn / emits broken .ics on a non-ISO date
items.why: calendar_event was the ONLY tool handler with no try/catch; gcalLink did new Date(startDate+T00:00:00Z).toISOString() which throws RangeError on a non-ISO date ("June 3") -> escaped runAgent + killed the whole turn. An unpadded "2026-6-3" produced a malformed DTSTART the calendar app silently dropped.
items.how: normalizeIsoDate (strict YYYY-MM-DD + round-trip validity) gates buildIcs/gcalLink so a bad date is dropped not thrown; dispatch wrapped in try/catch.

items.title: find_nearby / directions ignore the user coords when geocoding place names
items.why: "directions to Springfield" / "coffee near Washington" take Nominatim limit=1 (top global match) -> wrong city, no hint. The multi-candidate + near-bias fix applied to weather was never propagated; weatherCoords IS available in both handlers.
items.how: Bump nominatim to a few candidates + a pickNearest(coords) like weather.pickCandidate; pass deps.weatherCoords as the bias in the find_nearby + directions handlers.

items.title: find_nearby fixed 3km radius + no-area-found reads as "none nearby"
items.why: "nearest ER/hospital" returns "none nearby" when one exists just past 3km (dangerous false-negative); a failed area geocode is reported identically to genuinely-empty.
items.how: Expand the radius on an empty result (3->10->30km); distinguish a null geocode ("couldn t find that area") from empty results ("nothing within Nkm").

items.title: geo fetch helpers follow redirects without SSRF re-validation
items.why: defaultFetchText/Post use raw fetch redirect:follow, unlike scrape/fetch_json which re-check each hop via safeFetch. Hosts are hardcoded so low risk, but inconsistent with the SSRF discipline.
items.how: Route the geo GET/POST through safeFetch (redirect:manual + isUrlSafe per hop), or at least block non-https + private-IP redirects.

items.title: conditional multi-step recipe chaining
items.why: Recipes are one-shot; the biggest power multiplier (Instinct core) is chained steps where N feeds N+1 ("find cheapest flight to {city}, then weather+news there, then summarize") with an optional if/stop gate.
items.how: A chain recipe = ordered steps; run each, inject the prior output into the next task, optional contains/threshold gate to stop early. Mock-LLM testable.

items.title: starter recipe/template library (/templates)
items.why: The proactive retention flywheel (recipes/digests/alerts) never starts for a cold user — auto-suggest only fires on a REPEAT. A curated one-tap template pack seeds the first saved automation.
items.how: Static catalog (morning briefing, price watch, job-feed watch...) installed by name into the existing RecipeStore/DigestStore. Offline-testable.

items.title: scheduled chain ran literal; no step cap; if-gate negation match
items.why: Audit of just-shipped recipe-chaining found: a SCHEDULED chained recipe fired the literal "step1 >> step2" as ONE agent task (scheduler never called runChain) — silent daily wrong behavior; chains had no step cap (50 >> = 50 agent runs on one message); the if-gate matched its keyword as a bare substring so "if in stock" passed on "out of stock".
items.how: runChain dep on the schedule runner (chains fire as workflows); MAX_CHAIN_STEPS=6 cap in parseChainSteps; containsUnnegated for the if-gate.

items.title: chain: no progress ping + intermediate output sent as final
items.why: A multi-step chain awaits inline holding the per-chat lock with no "still working" ping (reads as a hang, wedges the queue); and a step that degrades/fails silently returns the PRIOR step output as if it were the complete answer.
items.how: Arm the progress-ping timer on the chain branch; when runChain stoppedEarly, prefix the result with a "couldn t finish all steps" note instead of passing it as final.

items.title: no live stock/equity quote tool
items.why: "whats Tesla at?"/"AAPL price" degrades to a slow flaky web_search+scrape; currency has a fast dedicated tool, stocks do not.
items.how: A get_quote tool over a keyless quote API (e.g. Stooq CSV or Yahoo quote JSON) via fetch_json; instant symbol->price.

items.title: first timed reminder fires at UTC + cryptic UTC-offset fix
items.why: A brand-new user "remind me at 7am" with no profile schedules at 7am UTC + is told to re-send /setlocation <city> UTC-5 (offset math they do not know); the canonical first errand silently misfires.
items.how: On a clock-time reminder with no tz set, ASK "what city are you in?" (stash the reminder, city->tz infer already exists) before scheduling, rather than scheduling-wrong-then-warning.

items.title: unified /dashboard of all automations
items.why: Schedules/recipes/digests/alerts are 4 separate list commands; a user loses track + stops adding. One rollup (next-fire, last-value/trend, status) is the retention surface.
items.how: Aggregate the existing stores into one /dashboard view; pure read.

items.title: pause/snooze an automation instead of deleting it
items.why: Only off-switch is /forget|/cancel which destroys the setup, so users delete configs they would keep through travel/noise.
items.how: A pausedUntil flag on schedule/alert; runner skips while paused; "snooze btc 3 days" / "resume btc".

items.title: List remove() substring match deletes neighbors
items.why: "remove milk" also nuked "almond milk"/"milk chocolate" — silent collateral loss on a store the user reads back.
items.how: Port notes.ts whole-word tiered matchScore into lists.ts remove().

items.title: Keyless dictionary/define tool
items.why: "define escrow"/"what does X mean" is a top phone errand; today answers from model memory (no source) or a slow scrape.
items.how: New src/lib/dictionary.ts hitting dictionaryapi.dev (keyless, injected fetch like fx/quote/crypto); parse+format definition/phonetics/synonyms; add define tool to agent + prompt + dispatch pin + help.

items.title: Time-in-city / timezone conversion
items.why: "what time is it in Tokyo"/"9am PT in London" before a call; agent guesses (often wrong) since datetime injection only covers the user own zone.
items.how: Deterministic IANA-offset math in a new lib (reuse profile CITY_TZ + DST-aware if feasible); a get_time/convert_time tool or handler branch; format both zones.

items.title: Handle forwarded PDF/CSV/image documents
items.why: Voice notes + photos are ingested but Telegram document attachments are not — a glaring asymmetry; "deal with this bill/statement" is a daily errand.
items.how: Wire Telegram document fileId download into the same treat-as-task path as photos; feed to existing pdf/extract/multimodal tooling.

items.title: atomicWriteJson swallows write failures → false confirms
items.why: On a full/unwritable disk Relay says "saved"/"reminder set" but nothing persisted; user never told, data vanishes on restart.
items.how: atomicWriteJson return success bool; callers surface a soft warning when a persist fails (schedule/notes/lists/profile/alerts).

items.title: SSRF DoH guard failed OPEN (drifted from mcp-forge fix)
items.why: Relay url-validator lagged a security fix (DEV-0211): hostResolvesToBlockedIp returned false on resolver error/timeout, so an attacker forcing a DoH timeout could reach an internal/metadata IP. Also broke the shared-lib parity guard (red before this run).
items.how: Backport mcp-forge fail-closed logic into relay copy: query() returns null on error, both-null -> block.

items.title: Save-confirmations still lie on write failure for 6 of 8 stores
items.why: The atomicWriteJson->bool hedge only reached Notes+Lists. ScheduleStore/AlertStore/RecipeStore/DigestStore/ProfileStore/BackgroundStore discard the return; add() confirms unconditionally. A reminder/alert/recipe that failed to persist still says "set" and vanishes on restart. Reminders are the highest-trust feature.
items.how: Make each persist() return the bool; thread saved into add/save methods with user-facing confirmations (schedule add, alert add, recipe save, digest define); hedge those handler confirmations like rememberFact/list-add already do.

items.title: Units default to imperial worldwide, wrong for ~95% of users
items.why: weatherUnits defaults imperial + find_nearby distances follow it; a London user first errand "weather in Paris" gets Fahrenheit unless they know to append (metric).
items.how: Infer metric/imperial from the resolved place country (US/liberia/myanmar imperial, else metric) when the user has not set a preference; keep explicit (metric)/(imperial) override.

items.title: Reminders before location capture fire at UTC silently
items.why: first-location-capture only triggers for weather/near-me, not the scheduler; "remind me at 9am" from a new user fires at 9am UTC with no warning it guessed the zone.
items.how: On the first clock/reminder task with no tz set, prompt once for city/UTC offset (mirror first-location-capture) or annotate the confirmation that it assumed UTC.

items.title: "Follow X" feed subscriptions (push new items)
items.why: Biggest retention lever + structurally distinct: alerts fire on value crossings, digests re-run recipes; neither pushes newly-published content. "follow this blog/subreddit/HN topic/YouTube channel".
items.how: Keyless RSS/Atom + Reddit .json + HN Firebase + YouTube channel feed; store last-seen ids per sub; ride schedule-runner + per-chat send-cap; ping only new entries (reuse feed-watch new-item keying).

items.title: Background errand completion clobbers interim conversation
items.why: dispatchBackground snapshots memory at dispatch, runs detached minutes, then memorySet([...staleSnapshot]) on completion — dropping every turn exchanged while waiting (which the bot explicitly invites).
items.how: On completion, re-read current memory + append the errand result instead of overwriting from the stale snapshot; or merge by message identity.

items.title: Feed watch marks >10 new items seen but shows only 10
items.why: Both feed paths showed the first 10 fresh items + "…and N more" but recordSeen committed ALL fresh keys, so items 11+ were marked seen and never surfaced — silently lost content on a busy feed (bug in the follow-feed code just shipped).
items.how: Record only the SHOWN items as seen; un-shown ones stay unseen and appear next check.

items.title: Feed dedup keys on title only
items.why: feedItemKey = normalized title (no url/id/date), so a recurring "Daily Discussion" thread or any repeated-headline post hashes to an already-seen key and is dropped forever; long titles sharing first 120 chars collide.
items.how: Include a URL/id/guid in the feed item + key on (title+link). parseFeed/parseXmlTitles must return {title,link}; feedItemKey uses the link when present.

items.title: Digest with all members transiently failing sends nothing
items.why: digest-runner returns null when no member is real; fireOne treats null as empty/deleted and stays silent — a bad-network morning makes a relied-upon briefing silently no-show, indistinguishable from deletion.
items.how: Distinguish transient all-fail from empty: send a brief "couldn't build your digest this morning (temporary)" note, or retry, instead of silent skip.

items.title: "once" clock reminders not tz-restamped on setlocation
items.why: restampTz recomputes daily/weekly only; a "remind me tomorrow at 8am" set before tz is fixed then corrected to UTC-5 fires at 3am local, once, silently.
items.how: Restamp future clock-time once reminders (dueMs derived from hourMin) to the new offset, like daily/weekly; skip pure relative/interval ones.

items.title: START copy sells a scraper, not a life assistant
items.why: START leads with HN/extract/screenshot/PDF, so a first-timer thinks it is a dev tool + never tries weather/remind/tip/near-me/scores; never told they can ask open questions or that sharing location unlocks weather/near-me.
items.how: Rewrite START to lead with everyday errands + "just ask" + the location unlock; keep power examples lower. Pure commands.ts copy.

items.title: Quiet-hours defers the alert CHECK, losing overnight crossings
items.why: A "below 50k" watch that crosses at 2am and reverts by the 8am quiet-end never fired — quiet-hours deferred the whole check, so the crossing was evaluated only at 8am (reverted).
items.how: Exempt alert: checks from the quiet-hours defer, mirroring the send-cap exemption; the check runs on cadence, only sends on a real change.

items.title: complete() ignores persist() bool -> once can double-fire after restart
items.why: On a full/unwritable disk a once reminder sends, is dropped only in memory, then re-fires after the next restart. Every other store hedges on lastSaveOk() but the proactive complete() path does not.
items.how: Have complete() surface the persist result; on a failed persist after a once fire, log + optionally flag so the runner can avoid a duplicate (or at least record it).

items.title: One hung proactive task delays every other chat’s due reminders
items.why: tick() is strictly sequential (for..await fireOne) with no per-task wall-clock timeout; a stalled anvil/LLM makes all other due reminders land late or miss the tick.
items.how: Wrap fireOne in a Promise.race timeout, or run due tasks via mapPool (as digest/watchlist already do), bounded so the anvil pool is safe.

items.title: Corrupt store file silently wipes a chat’s automations
items.why: readJsonSafe backs up + returns null; the store loads empty so every reminder/alert/recipe/digest vanishes with only an operator log — user never told.
items.how: Surface a user-facing "your saved items couldn’t be loaded (backed up)" notice, or refuse-to-serve that store until acknowledged, instead of silently starting empty.

items.title: No live sports scores (promised in prompt, unbacked)
items.why: SYSTEM_PROMPT advertises "who won the game" but there is no tool; falls to a flaky scrape of JS scoreboards. Keyless ESPN scoreboard JSON exists.
items.how: New src/lib/scores.ts hitting a keyless ESPN scoreboard endpoint; parse team+score+status; get_score tool + dispatch + prompt + help.

items.title: Contacts book so "text mom" drafts to a saved recipient
items.why: compose only works if the user re-types a raw email/number every time; "text mom" dead-ends asking for the address. Its highest-intent use silently fails.
items.how: A small name->handle store (like notes/lists); compose resolves a saved contact by name; "save mom’s number as ..." to add. Feeds the deferred confirm-to-send.

items.title: Timed-out fire still sends when it finishes late (double ping)
items.why: withFireTimeout (shipped last run) abandoned but did not cancel a slow fire: the timeout advanced/failed the schedule, then the original run finished and ALSO sent + completed -> duplicate/late ping + a false "your watch is failing" receipt after 3 slow fires.
items.how: Thread an isCancelled flag into fireOne; the timeout flips it; guard send + every complete() so a late finish is dropped.

items.title: atomicWriteJson never fsyncs (torn file on power loss)
items.why: Header claims temp+fsync+rename but there is no fsync — a hard crash/power-loss can persist the rename while the tmp contents are unflushed, producing the empty/torn file the module exists to prevent, which then trips the corrupt path + wipes a store.
items.how: openSync the tmp, writeSync, fsyncSync, close, then rename; optionally fsync the dir. Keep never-throws + return bool.

items.title: Contact fuzzy match can draft to the wrong person confidently
items.why: ContactStore.get word-overlap fallback (longest-name-wins) resolves "text mom" to "mom's doctor" when there is no exact "mom"; formatDraft shows a confident To: line -> one tap from texting the wrong person.
items.how: Only fuzzy-match when unambiguous (single hit) OR the query token equals a whole word of exactly one contact; else return null (ask which). Mirror the recipe slotsAmbiguous guard.

items.title: On-demand news headlines (promised, unbacked)
items.why: START advertises "every morning: weather + top news" but there is no news source; "what's the news" runs a slow scrape. feeds.ts (RSS/Reddit/HN) infra already exists to reuse.
items.how: New get_news tool over a keyless headline feed (Reuters/AP/BBC RSS or HN front page); parse top N titles; tool + dispatch + prompt + help. Reuse parseXmlItems.

items.title: City,Region tz guess wrong when region unknown (San Jose, Costa Rica -> PT)
items.why: inferTzFromLocation falls back to the leftmost known city token when the region tail is not in the table, so "San Jose, Costa Rica" resolves to California (UTC-8) and reminders fire 2h off — the fn contract promised "never guesses wrong".
items.how: When a comma region tail is present but unknown, do NOT fall back to a bare city token that is a US-city collision; leave tz unset (ask) instead.

items.title: Future-day weather silently shows today
items.why: resolveWhen ignored "next" + returned [0] when the named weekday == today, and formatWeatherWhen returned null for an out-of-window day -> agent silently rendered TODAY for a future question. The tool literally advertises "the RIGHT day, not today".
items.how: resolveWhen: "next <weekday>" -> +7 (no today collision); return the index even past the window. formatWeatherWhen: an out-of-window day returns an honest "beyond my N-day forecast" note, never today.

items.title: Ambiguous team name returns the wrong sport confidently
items.why: TEAM_LEAGUE maps giants->mlb, rangers->nhl, kings->nba unconditionally, so "did the Giants win" always answers SF Giants (never NFL), "Rangers" always NHL (never Texas Rangers MLB) — a confident wrong answer, no hedge.
items.how: Drop the genuinely-ambiguous team names from TEAM_LEAGUE (or require the league/sport word in-query); resolveLeague then returns null for a bare ambiguous team -> agent asks which.

items.title: A due daily digest is silently dropped when over the hourly cap
items.why: Only once-reminders (grace-defer) + alert-checks are cap-exempt; a daily/digest: over the cap hits safeComplete+continue and vanishes for the day with only an operator log — the relied-upon morning briefing just no-shows.
items.how: Give a daily/digest the same defer-past-cap grace as a once (leave due, retry next tick) instead of dropping the occurrence; or exempt digests like alert-checks.

items.title: Concurrent sync turn erases a background errand's memory
items.why: The errand-completion path now re-reads memory, but the INBOUND sync turn still writes [...snapshot] captured before its agent ran; if an errand finishes mid-turn (the ack invites more texts), the sync write erases the errand turn -> a follow-up has no memory of it.
items.how: Apply the same re-read-before-write discipline on the sync path (or serialize via the per-chat chain), so neither side clobbers the other.

items.title: chart_it — texted graph of tracked/numeric data
items.why: Watch/alert trend series + any numeric answer come back as a wall of numbers; a chart image is the natural payoff for stored history + a free-infra edge no vendor-browser competitor matches.
items.how: Keyless quickchart.io URL -> image via the existing screenshot/doc attachment path; a chart tool + dispatch that plots a watch series or an ad-hoc number set.

items.title: Named team not playing -> dumps every other game as the answer
items.why: filterByTeam falls back to the whole slate on a no-match, so "did the Lakers win" on a Lakers-idle night returned Celtics/Heat/etc as scores to report, confidently answering about teams never asked.
items.how: resolveLeague marks viaTeam; getScores checks teamMatchedAny and returns {games:[],teamNotPlaying:true} when a named team has no game today; dispatch says they are not playing instead of listing others.

items.title: No calculator (chained/financial math answered inline, silently wrong)
items.why: SYSTEM_PROMPT routes ALL arithmetic/tips/percentages/date-math to inline LLM answering with no verification; "split $127.50 3 ways with 20% tip" / "monthly payment on a $30k loan at 6% for 5y" get confident wrong numbers — the highest-frequency errand class through an unverified path.
items.how: New src/lib/calc.ts: a safe arithmetic evaluator (no eval; tokenize + shunting-yard, + - * / % ^ parens, %, basic fns) + a calc tool; route money/percent/loan math to it. Reject anything non-numeric.

items.title: Scheduled digest "more"/"link" pages the TRIMMED copy
items.why: A long scheduled digest is trimmed before send but recordSend caches only the trimmed text, so "more" says "nothing more to show" (a lie) + "link" cannot return a URL from a cut line. Inbound /run digest stores the untrimmed parts.full and works — an asymmetry.
items.how: Thread the untrimmed composed digest text into recordSend on the scheduled path (schedule-runner), so the ping cache holds full + sent like the inbound path.

items.title: Agent-driven feed watch false-fires on prose rewording
items.why: extractListItems keeps any non-bullet non-colon line as a feed item; an agent reply that is a plain sentence gets keyed by feedItemKey, so a reworded same-fact next check reads as "1 new" — crying wolf on the agent-driven alert.feed path (the keyless feedSource path is safe, uses stable ids).
items.how: Require an actual list shape (bullet/ordinal, >=2 items) before treating a reply as a feed; else fall back to change-detection for prose.

items.title: When-then: run a recipe/errand on an alert fire (not just notify)
items.why: Alerts fire + recipes run + one scheduler drives both, but they are wired only to NOTIFY; "when BTC below 55k run my rebalance-check" would convert every passive watch into IFTTT-style action — the biggest do-more unlock vs Instinct.
items.how: Extend alert def with an optional then-recipe; on fire, invoke the named recipe (reuse recipeResolve/runChain) + include/deliver its result. Guard against slotted recipes (needs a value).

items.title: Error path clobbers interim/errand memory from stale snapshot
items.why: The handler catch wrote [...history,...] from the pre-run snapshot; a background errand (or interim turn) that wrote memory while the run was in flight got erased when the run then threw — the exact race the success path was already fixed for.
items.how: Re-read current memory in the catch (memoryGet -> append), mirroring the success path.

items.title: Team-not-playing guard bypassed when the query also names a league
items.why: The not-playing guard only triggers on ref.viaTeam, but resolveLeague matches the LEAGUES word first, so "did the Lakers win, NBA scores?" resolves without viaTeam -> filterByTeam dumps the whole slate again.
items.how: In getScores run teamMatchedAny whenever the query names a KNOWN team (independent of how the league resolved), not only on viaTeam; return teamNotPlaying when it names a team with no game.

items.title: reminderOnly fire path lacks isCancelled guard -> duplicate reminder
items.why: fireOne main send + alert-silent + digest-null all check isCancelled() before side effects (timeout late-finish guard), but the reminderOnly branch awaits send + completes with no check, so a send stalling past the 90s timeout gets retried while the original lands late -> double meds reminder.
items.how: Add an isCancelled() check before the reminderOnly send + complete, like the other fire paths.

items.title: chart/trend series poisoned by a spurious number in a non-degraded error reply
items.why: recordPoint runs before the numberless/baseline-protection guards + only skips on null extractValue; a non-degraded reply like "the page returned a 404" yields 404, stored in the series chart/trend read -> a bogus spike.
items.how: Move recordPoint after the numberless guard, or skip recording when the reply matches an error-ish shape / when extractValue would also fail the baseline guard.

items.title: Translate-anything tool (text or a page)
items.why: Translation is a top assistant ask + a glaring gap next to define-a-word; only implicit inline now (no consistency, no discoverability, weak on long text / pages).
items.how: A translate tool: for pasted text, LLM-translate inline with the target language; for a URL, scrape then translate. Add tool + prompt + help. Optionally romaji/pronunciation like define.

items.title: Profile (location/tz) save failure silently swallowed
items.why: ProfileStore was the one store whose handler never checked lastSaveOk(); a failed location/tz write confirmed "saved" then reverted to UTC on restart -> every weather/near-me + daily-reminder time silently wrong (the wrong-hour reminder bug through the back door).
items.how: Thread profiles.lastSaveOk() through setLocation + captureLocation; handler hedges the confirmation when saved===false, like every other store.

items.title: Real unit/measurement conversion (temp/weight/length/volume/cooking)
items.why: "180C to F", "5ft11 in cm", "2 cups flour in grams" fall to model memory (prompt literally says "oz in a cup = 8") — a correctness risk the prompt itself calls silently-wrong for multi-step. Only currency has a real convert tool.
items.how: New src/lib/units-convert.ts: deterministic conversion tables (temp/mass/length/volume + common cooking) + a convert tool mirroring convert_currency; parse "N <unit> to <unit>". Reject unknown units.

items.title: Cooking recipes / meal ideas by ingredient
items.why: "dinner ideas with eggs, spinach, feta" / "what can I make with chicken" is a top everyday ask; falls to a slow blog-link web_search AND the word "recipe" collides with the automation-recipe system.
items.how: Keyless TheMealDB (filter.php?i=ingredient, random.php, lookup.php) -> a meal-ideas tool; parse ingredients; format name + a few + a link. Distinct verb from automation recipes.

items.title: Sunrise/sunset/daylight times
items.why: profile.ts already treats "sunset today"/"is it dark by 7" as location errands but no tool returns them -> degrades to weather/web_search.
items.how: Open-Meteo daily sunrise/sunset (already the weather provider) -> a suntimes tool or a get_weather field; format for the resolved place + day.

items.title: Translate grabs the first in/to as the target, not the final language
items.why: The target regex matched the FIRST "in/to" and lazily ran to end-of-string, so "I want to go to the beach to Spanish" gave target "go to the beach to Spanish" -> a bogus language + mangled source, surfaced as an authoritative translation (silent-wrong).
items.how: Anchor the target to the FINAL "to/into/in <lang>" clause at end-of-string; strip only that matched clause from the body.

items.title: Sunrise/sunset refuses a located user for evening/winter phrasings
items.why: Dispatch hasPlace=/ ins+[A-Za-z]/ fires on "in the evening"/"in winter", so it passes only near + drops lat/lng; sunPlace then rejects those tails -> no place, no coords -> "ask which city" even though coords are saved.
items.how: Make the dispatch use the SAME place-detection as sunPlace (call sunPlace on the request): only treat as named-place when sunPlace returns non-null; else pass coords directly.

items.title: Cooking "1 cup to oz" fails as cross-type
items.why: Bare "oz" maps only to mass; "cup" is volume -> the canonical kitchen conversion hits the dim-mismatch reject. The tool cant do the thing its header cites as motivation.
items.how: When one side is a volume unit + the other is bare "oz"/"ounce", treat oz as fluid ounce (volume). Or detect a volume context (cup/tbsp/tsp/ml/l/pint) and map oz->fl oz.

items.title: calc bare % modulo dead + min/max with 3+ args errors
items.why: The bare-percent rewrite eats every literal % before the modulo op tokenizes ("17 % 5" -> malformed); toRpn tracks no function arity so "max(1,2,3)" leaves residue -> malformed. Both advertised.
items.how: Only rewrite % as percent when NOT between two numbers as an operator (or require "mod" and drop % from the advertised op list); track function arity in toRpn so min/max fold N args.

items.title: "open now" filtering for near-me
items.why: "pharmacy near me" at 9pm sends you to one that closed at 6 — Relay passes OSM opening_hours raw and never computes open/closed vs the user local time.
items.how: Parse OSM opening_hours vs the chat local time (coords/profile known); mark each place open/closed now + sort/filter open-first; note when hours are unknown.

items.title: scheduled recipe/reminder replies trim to 1200 chars, tail unrecoverable
items.why: schedule-runner passes the already-trimmed formatReply(res.reply) as both sent and full text, so a long scheduled/recipe answer arrives cut off and 'more' says 'that's the whole answer' — dropped content is gone. The digest path was fixed (fullText) but the plain scheduled-agent + recipe path wasn't.
items.how: Use formatReplyParts to keep the untrimmed text and pass it as `full` to recordSend (mirror the digest fix) so chunkFrom can serve the tail on 'more'. Offline test: mock send + a >1200-char reply, assert 'more' returns the remainder.

items.title: quiet-hours defers explicit one-shot alarms/reminders past their exact time
items.why: schedule-runner applies the quiet-hours deferTo to every non-alert schedule including `once` clock-time tasks, so 'wake me at 6am' inside the quiet window is pushed to the window end and fires late — defeats an alarm.
items.how: Exempt kind==='once' (at least clockTime ones) from the quiet-hours defer, mirroring the alert-check exemption already present. Offline test: mock clock + a once inside the quiet window fires at its time, not deferred.

items.title: no date/calendar math (days-until, day-of-week, age, date diff)
items.why: 'how many days until Christmas', 'what day is July 4th', 'how old if born 1990', 'days between two dates' have no home — calc is arithmetic-only, so these fall to a slow browse or a hallucinated guess. Very high everyday frequency.
items.how: Add a keyless deterministic date tool (parse common date phrases + relative like 'next friday'; compute diff/day-of-week/age) beside get_time/calculate. Pure, offline-testable. New TOOLS[] entry + dispatch + prompt line + HELP + sorted tool-list test.

items.title: acknowledged / escalating reminders (re-ping until user replies done)
items.why: A reminder fires once and is easily missed; the biggest daily-habit hook (meds, water, standup) is a reminder that re-pings on an interval until acknowledged. Turns a one-off into a daily reason to open the chat.
items.how: Add a 'sticky: re-fire every N min until 'done'/'stop', cap M times' flag to schedule.ts + a done/stop handler branch. Fully offline-testable with a mock clock. Reuses existing schedule fire plumbing.

items.title: a single "done" cancels EVERY sticky reminder, not the one that pinged
items.why: acknowledgeSticky removes ALL of a chat's sticky reminders on any ack; a user who replies 'done' to the meds nag silently loses their unrelated 'drink water every 30m' sticky too. Regression in the just-shipped sticky feature — exactly the black hole it was meant to prevent.
items.how: Track the most-recently-FIRED sticky per chat (store lastFiredMs or a fired-order marker); scope the ack to it (or match by task text when the ack names one). Fall back to all only if there's a single sticky. Offline test: two stickies, ack after one fires -> only that one removed.

items.title: transient send outage burns a sticky reminder’s fire budget + can self-drop it unseen
items.why: On a send throw the tick catch treats an interval sticky like any recurring: complete() increments stickyFired and can reach stickyMax + splice it. Unlike a 'once' (which retries on transient failure), a sticky's count advances on DELIVERY failure — so a brief Telegram/anvil outage can silently exhaust + delete a 'nag me until done' the user never saw ping once.
items.how: Only advance stickyFired after a CONFIRMED send (mirror the once transient-retry path): on a failed fire, don't count it toward the cap; retry next tick. Offline test: a sticky whose send throws N times doesn't lose fire budget + survives.

items.title: no hourly / rain-timing weather ("will it rain this afternoon / at 3pm?")
items.why: weather.ts fetches only Open-Meteo current+daily, so a time-of-day question ('umbrella this afternoon?', 'rain tonight?') gets a whole-day max-precip guess, not WHEN. One of the highest-frequency first errands.
items.how: Add &hourly=precipitation_probability,temperature_2m to the existing keyless Open-Meteo call + a pure 'next-N-hours' formatter; detect a time-of-day phrase to pick the window. Reuses saved location. Offline-testable with a fixture.

items.title: no air-quality / UV tool ("is the air OK to run", "need sunscreen?")
items.why: 'is the air bad / smoky', 'UV today / do I need sunscreen' fall through to a flaky web_search/scrape; no AQI/UV tool exists. High seasonal/health value.
items.how: New tool near weather: Open-Meteo air-quality API is keyless + takes the same lat/lng weather already resolves+stores per-chat. Fetch + pure formatter + unit tests, mirroring weather.ts. New TOOLS[] entry + dispatch + prompt line + HELP + sorted tool-list test.

items.title: cancel/forget/remove/clear confirm success even when the disk write failed
items.why: The SAVE path hedges ('couldn't save to disk') via atomicWriteJson's bool + lastSaveOk, but the DELETE path doesn't: schedule.remove/notes.forget+clear/lists.remove+clear/contacts.forget all drop persist()'s return. So 'cancel my 3pm reminder' / 'forget I'm allergic to peanuts' / 'forget everything about me' get a clean confirm, but on a failed write the data resurrects on restart — a cancelled reminder fires again, a deleted privacy fact keeps getting injected into answers. Worse than a failed save because the user believes it's done.
items.how: Plumb the persist bool through the destructive paths (return removed+saved, mirror the add-side pattern) so the handler hedges ('I removed it for now but couldn't save the change to disk — try again'). Cover schedule cancel, forgetFact/clear, list remove/clear, contact forget. Offline-testable with an unwritable store (parent-is-a-file trick already used in tests).

items.title: a wall-clock "once" set before location fires at the wrong hour, never re-stamped
items.why: restampTz recomputes daily/weekly on setlocation but EXCLUDES `once` (comment claims a clock once 'fires just once shortly anyway' — false for 'remind me tomorrow at 8am'). Its dueMs was baked as an absolute instant at offset 0, so after the user sets US-Eastern it still fires at 8am UTC = 3am local, with no warning. Distinct from the parked DST issue — a create-before-location ordering bug.
items.how: In restampTz, also re-stamp clockTime `once` schedules whose dueMs is future: shift the UTC instant by the offset delta (same math as the daily/weekly branch) so it keeps the intended wall-clock time. clockTime already flags these. Offline test: create a clock once at offset 0, restamp to -300, assert dueMs shifts to hold local 8am.

items.title: no QR-code generation ("make a QR for this link / my wifi")
items.why: 'make a QR code for this link' floods into a floundering browse or refusal, though the sendPhoto image channel is already wired. High-delight, instant proof the bot does real work.
items.how: Add a keyless QR tool: build a chart/QR image URL (quickchart.io/qr or api.qrserver.com — already keyless img sources) or generate offline; return the PNG via the existing chart/sendPhoto path. New TOOLS[] entry + dispatch + prompt + HELP + sorted tool-list test. Offline-test the URL/payload builder.

items.title: feedItemKey truncates to 120 chars — distinct long titles collide, a new item never pings
items.why: feedItemKey = normalizeForCompare(item).slice(0,120). Two different feed entries sharing a 120-char prefix (verbose news/marketplace titles) get the same dedup key; the second is treated as already-seen and never surfaces — a job/listing/headline the user waits for silently never pings, reads as 'nothing new'.
items.how: Key on a stable id when present (the follow-feed path already does; the agent-driven checkAlert path keys title-only), else hash the FULL normalized title instead of a 120-char prefix slice. Offline test: two titles sharing a long prefix get distinct keys.

items.title: error-shaped agent replies false-fire alert triggers + poison the baseline
items.why: alert-runner imports looksLikeErrorReply but only uses it to skip recording a time-series point — NOT in the trigger decision. A soft-failure reply like 'the page returned a 404' yields extractValue()=404 (not null, so the numberless guard misses it), satisfies a 'below 50000' predicate/threshold, and pings a false alarm showing an error string as the value; on a threshold it poisons the baseline so the next check re-fires. Hits watchlist members + follow-feed value paths too.
items.how: Treat looksLikeErrorReply(value) as indeterminate (hold, keep last-good baseline, don't fire) in the same spots the degraded flag is already checked — conditionHolds predicate eval + the threshold changed()/numberless block + the watchlist changed() path. Offline test: an error-shaped reply doesn't fire + doesn't advance the baseline.

items.title: digest presents a soft-error reply as real briefing content
items.why: digest-runner only demotes a member to '(couldn't fetch)' when the agent throws or sets degraded. A non-degraded reply whose TEXT is a fetch failure ('btc: the page returned a 404') becomes a 'real' section verbatim, and the all-fail-vs-partial logic miscounts it as real content so the honest 'every source failed' notice never fires. User reads an error line as fact.
items.how: Gate the digest member line with looksLikeErrorReply (already in alerts.ts) the same way degraded is — demote to '(couldn't fetch)' + count it as a failure for the all-fail/partial tally. Offline test: an error-text member is demoted + a digest of all-error members emits the all-failed notice.

items.title: alertEdit confirms "Updated" without checking the disk write
items.why: Every other write path surfaces lastSaveOk() + hedges (persist-bool-all-stores effort), but index.ts alertEdit returns {ok,name,summary} with no saved field + handler confirms unconditionally. A failed write silently reverts the trigger to the old threshold on restart — user watches the wrong number with no warning. AlertStore.updateTrigger already persists + lastSaveOk exists.
items.how: Return saved from alertEdit (alerts.lastSaveOk()) + hedge in the handler ('I couldn't save that to disk') exactly like alertDefine/scheduleAdd. Offline test: a failed-write edit hedges.

items.title: no monthly/yearly recurring reminders ("pay rent on the 1st", "mom’s birthday every year")
items.why: The schedule parser supports only once/daily/weekly/interval, so the two most universal recurring errands — monthly bills + annual birthdays — silently fall back to a one-time or misparsed reminder. Reminders are the core retention hook.
items.how: Add 'monthly'/'yearly' ScheduleKinds + parse ('every month on the 1st', 'every year on <date>', 'monthly', 'annually') + a complete()/nextMonthlyMs/nextYearlyMs roll-forward reusing the absolute-date month roll + short-month clamp already in schedule.ts. Offline-testable with a fixed clock. New kind must thread the cue set + tz-restamp + dashboard.

items.title: monthly reminder on day 29/30/31 silently skips every short month
items.why: domAtMs requires new Date(atUser).getUTCDate()===day, so 'pay rent on the 31st every month' fires only in the 7 months with a 31st (skips Feb/Apr/Jun/Sep/Nov); 'on the 30th' skips Feb. User is confirmed 'I'll do this every month' but gets NO reminder for ~5 bill cycles a year, silently. complete() reschedules through the same fn so it repeats forever. Regression in the just-shipped monthly kind.
items.how: For monthly, clamp the day to the month's LAST day instead of skipping (Feb 31 -> Feb 28/29, Apr 31 -> Apr 30). Add a monthly-specific next-occurrence that clamps rather than reusing domAtMs's skip semantics (keep domAtMs as-is for the absolute 'on the Nth' one-shot). Offline test: 'on the 31st' fires end-of-Feb + Apr30, never skips.

items.title: monthly/yearly reminder dropped for the whole period if over the hourly send-cap
items.why: schedule-runner graceEligible = kind==='once' || isDigest; monthly/yearly fall into the else branch that safeCompletes (advances the recurrence) when over-cap — like a harmless daily. But a monthly/yearly is a single high-stakes promise per period: if the chat is over-cap the morning rent/birthday is due, THIS month's/year's reminder is lost + the next is 30/365 days out.
items.how: Add monthly/yearly to graceEligible so they get the defer-then-force grace a 'once' gets (retry until a slot frees, force past the grace window) instead of being dropped. Offline test: a monthly over-cap defers, not drops.

items.title: yearly reminder on Feb 29 (+ invalid Feb 30/Jun 31) fires the wrong day, mislabeled
items.why: dateAtMs has no getUTCDate()===day validity check (unlike domAtMs), and the yearly parser accepts any day 1-31 for any month. 'birthday every year on Feb 29' fires Mar 1 in non-leap years; 'Feb 30'/'June 31' silently fire Mar 2/Jul 1. The reminder header shows the date the user asked for, so the mistimed ping looks authoritative.
items.how: For yearly, snap Feb 29 -> Feb 28 in non-leap years (clamp to month-end, same fix as monthly) and REJECT an impossible month/day pair at parse time (Feb 30, Jun 31) so it doesn't silently become a wrong-day yearly. Offline test: Feb 29 yearly fires Feb 28 in a non-leap year; 'Feb 30' is rejected.

items.title: inbound photo is one-shot describe, never chains into a tool
items.why: The inbound-photo path (handler -> describeImage) returns a vision string straight to formatReply, never entering the agent tool loop — so 'split this receipt 3 ways +20% tip' / 'convert these menu prices to USD' / 'what's the cheapest veg dish' answer from the model's own guesswork instead of calling calculate/convert/translate (the exact silent-math error the text path forbids).
items.how: Route the extracted image text/caption back through runAgent (as a normal turn with the vision content as context) so a photo can chain into calculate/translate/convert_units/find_nearby. Offline-testable by feeding a fixed vision string into the agent loop + asserting the tool call. Keep a plain 'describe' when there's no actionable ask.

items.title: no timer ("set a timer for 20 minutes", "timer 10 min")
items.why: parseSchedule handles 'in N min' + 'alarm at HH' but the word 'timer' + the 'for N minutes' duration form have NO branch — the single most common phone-assistant errand silently falls through to the agent (no timer tool) and returns a confused/refusing reply.
items.how: Add a timer parse branch ("set a timer for X", "timer X min", "for N minutes") -> a once + reminderOnly schedule with a 'timer done' note (reuse the existing infra). Offline-testable with a fixed clock. Thread the cue set.

items.title: a reminder with no time given is silently dropped, never set
items.why: 'remind me to call mom' (no when-clause) fails parseSchedule (empty time clause) so it's never stored + drops to the agent (no reminder tool) — the user believes a reminder is set when nothing was. A trust-killing silent failure on the core feature.
items.how: Detect a reminder shape with a missing time and ask one 'when should I remind you?', stashing + re-running like the pending-location clarify flow already in the handler. Deterministic, offline-testable.

items.title: no generic "tell me when THIS page changes" watcher
items.why: alerts watch numeric thresholds + feeds watch new items, but there's no 'notify on ANY change to this URL' — restocks, price drops with no fixed number, status/policy/appointment pages. A killer generic capability that turns Relay from a reader into a stakeout.
items.how: Store a content-hash + a text snapshot from the existing anvil scrape; on the alert-runner cadence, re-scrape, compare (pure hash + text-diff), notify only on a real diff (show what changed). Keyless, offline-testable (hash+diff are pure).

items.title: can generate QR but can’t READ one from a sent photo
items.why: make_qr generates QR codes but a user who photographs a QR poster / product barcode and asks 'what is this / open this' gets the generic vision describe, which can't reliably decode the payload — the errand dead-ends. Natural symmetric complement to make_qr + the new photo-to-action pipeline.
items.how: Keyless local decode (jsQR/quirc-style) on the already-downloaded image bytes -> the URL/wifi/text payload; hook the photo branch. Offline-testable against fixture images.

items.title: watch-any-page on a dynamic page pings every check, bypassing cap + quiet hours
items.why: A page that legitimately changes every load (nonce/CSRF token, embedded timestamp, 'X min ago', rotating ad) makes diffPages see a change on EVERY fetch, so the watch fires each scheduler tick — including 3am. Alerts are EXEMPT from the anti-spam cap AND quiet-hours defer (premise: 'an alert only sends on a rare real change'), which is FALSE for page-diff — the one watch type that can flap is the one allowed to storm. Regression in the just-shipped watch-any-page.
items.how: Add a flap guard: track consecutive-change count per page watch; after N straight changes (e.g. 3), auto-mute or downgrade to 'this page changes constantly — stop watching?' instead of pinging. Alternatively strip volatile tokens (digits/timestamps) harder in pageText before diffing. Offline test: a page that changes every fetch stops pinging after the cap.

items.title: page-diff snapshot stored uncapped — a big page bloats the whole alerts store
items.why: The page snapshot is stored as lastValue with NO cap, unlike MAX_SERIES_POINTS(400) + MAX_SEEN_KEYS(200). A big page (long terms/policy/search-results, hundreds of KB) inflates every atomic rewrite of the shared alerts file; on a constrained disk the write starts failing and atomicWriteJson failure means EVERY user's alerts silently stop persisting.
items.how: Cap the stored page snapshot to the first N KB (e.g. slice to ~16KB of normalized text) in the page-diff branch before setLast, mirroring the series/seen caps. Offline test: a huge page's stored snapshot is bounded.

items.title: seconds-granularity timers silently rounded up to a full minute
items.why: 'timer for 20 seconds' fires at 60s; 'timer for 90 seconds' at 120s. schedule.ts rounds sec -> Math.max(MINUTE, round(n/60)*MINUTE), a materially wrong duration confirmed as if correct. Short timers (egg, plank, steep) are among the most common.
items.how: Honor sub-minute timers honestly if the runner tick allows (or) tell the user 'my shortest timer is 1 minute' instead of silently reshaping. Prefer honest sub-minute if schedule tick granularity permits; else disclose. Offline test: 20s either fires ~20s or the confirm says it was rounded.

items.title: no instant joke / fun-fact / trivia (common first message)
items.why: 'tell me a joke' / 'fun fact' / 'trivia question' — among the most common literal FIRST messages to a new bot — fall to a slow 10-30s browse or a stale from-memory answer. The first delightful instant reply earns a real errand next.
items.how: Add a keyless get_fun tool (official-joke-api / uselessfacts / opentdb). Fetch + format, offline-testable with fixtures. New TOOLS[] entry + dispatch + prompt + HELP + sorted tool-list test.

items.title: looksLikeErrorReply swallows real alert/feed changes containing common words
items.why: ERROR_REPLY_RE ends with bare  error  + lone words (cannot/blocked/failed/unavailable/no results) that occur constantly in legitimate content. It gates EVERY non-page value path + each watchlist member, so a HN/news headline watch on 'Why you cannot trust AI benchmarks' / 'Tesla recall blocked by court' / 'No results found' is treated as a fetch failure, held at the old baseline, and goes DARK on that change forever. My error-reply-false-fires fix over-reached.
items.how: Anchor the regex to real failure PHRASING (couldn't load / unable to load / error 4xx-5xx / returned a 500 / request failed / timed out), not lone words mid-sentence. Keep catching the soft-failure prose it was built for. Offline test: legit headlines with 'cannot/blocked/error' are NOT flagged; 'the page returned a 404' still is.

items.title: pageWatchUrl keeps trailing punctuation -> dead page watch
items.why: pageWatchUrl captures https?://S+ up to whitespace, so 'watch terms: https://site/policy.' stores the literal URL with the trailing period -> every fetch 404s -> pagediff silent branch forever. User is told 'Watching...' but never pinged. A black hole on the just-shipped watch-any-page.
items.how: Trim trailing sentence punctuation + a dangling close-paren/bracket from the captured URL (mirror last-result.extractLinks which already does this). Offline test: a URL with a trailing period/paren yields the clean URL.

items.title: page-diff stableText masks meaningful times -> appointment/status page never pings
items.why: stableText masks ALL clock times + ISO timestamps to stop volatile 'last updated' flap, but that erases CONTENT-bearing times: 'Next available: 3:15pm'->'5:45pm' or 'Departs 9:00'->'10:30' mask to the same key, and pageKey equality short-circuits before diffPages runs. The appointment/departure watch — the module's advertised use case — goes silent on exactly the change it's for.
items.how: Narrow the volatile-time mask to times that co-occur with a volatile lead-in ('last updated'/'as of'/'N ago'/a timestamp label), not every bare time on the page. Or diff the RAW text (unmasked) once pageKey says changed, and only use the mask to gate the flap counter. Offline test: 'Next available 3:15pm'->'5:45pm' registers as a change; a 'last updated 3:15pm' churn does not.

items.title: "pollen today" matches air-quality intent but pollen is never fetched
items.why: airquality.ts isAirRequest regex includes 'pollen' -> routes to get_air_quality, but the Open-Meteo query only requests us_aqi/pm2_5/pm10/ozone/uv — no pollen fields. An allergy sufferer asking 'pollen today' gets AQI+UV + zero pollen. Matched then silently dropped.
items.how: Add pollen fields (alder/birch/grass/ragweed) to the Open-Meteo air-quality query + a formatter line; caveat that pollen is Europe-only (US -> nulls, say so) rather than promising it globally. Offline-testable with a fixture. Lower rank: Europe-only coverage.

items.title: re-defining a watch by name leaves stale pageUrl/series/flapCount -> wrong type + blended history
items.why: AlertStore.add's overwrite branch mutates a hand-picked subset (task/threshold/condition/then/feed/feedSource/members) and NEVER touches pageUrl, series, or flapCount. So: (a) re-defining an existing name AS a page-watch stores task=URL but pageUrl=undefined -> runner runs the LLM on a bare URL instead of page-diffing (confirmation says 'watching that page', does something else); (b) re-pointing a former page-watch to a value task leaves the stale pageUrl -> keeps diffing the OLD page forever; (c) 'watch price: bitcoin' redefined to 'silver' keeps the old BTC series so the chart/trend shows a phantom crash (60000->30). Confirmation contradicts behavior — the exact saved-but-broken trust failure guarded elsewhere.
items.how: In the overwrite branch set existing.pageUrl = a.pageUrl (undefined clears it), and when the task/trigger/pageUrl changes, reset lastValue + series + flapCount + seen so a redefine starts fresh (matches the feed/feedSource reset already there). Offline test: redefine name as page-watch -> pageUrl set + series cleared; redefine off page-watch -> pageUrl cleared.

items.title: "do I need sunscreen" answers from the instant UV, not the day’s peak
items.why: formatAirQuality prints the current uv_index with no time qualifier, so 'UV today / do I need sunscreen' at 8am reads the morning value (2 -> low, no sunscreen) even when midday peaks at 9 (very high); at night it reads 0. The headline sunscreen use case gets a confidently misleading 'you're fine' for a whole-day plan.
items.how: Fetch daily=uv_index_max from Open-Meteo (forecast API — the air-quality API may not expose it; add a second field or a small forecast call) and lead the sunscreen guidance off the DAILY PEAK ('peaks at UV 9 around midday — wear sunscreen'), labeling the current reading 'right now'. Offline-testable with a fixture. Or, cheap partial: label the current value 'right now' so it's not read as the day's answer.

items.title: no "every weekday at 9" cadence — degrades to daily (fires weekends) or one weekday
items.why: Reminders support once/daily/weekly/interval/monthly/yearly but not Mon-Fri, so 'remind me every weekday at 5 to log my timesheet' mis-schedules (daily fires Sat/Sun, or a single weekly day). 'weekday'/'weekdays'/'workdays' is the single most common recurring work cadence people say — a top first-week action.
items.how: parseSchedule ALREADY maps 'weekday'->[1,2,3,4,5] and 'weekend'->[0,6] in the weekly branch (weeklyClause). Verify it actually reaches a weekly schedule + fires only on those days (audit implies it degrades — check the cue/branch order). If already correct, this is a done-noop; else route 'every weekday at N' to a weekly with weekdays [1-5]. Offline test: 'every weekday at 9' -> weekly, weekdays [1,2,3,4,5].

items.title: no unit-price "better buy" compare ("500g for $4 or 1.2kg for $9?")
items.why: 'which is cheaper, 500g for $4 or 1.2kg for $9' has no owner — calculate does raw arithmetic + convert_units converts measures, but nothing normalizes to price-per-unit + names the winner, so the agent hand-normalizes mixed units (the silently-wrong mental math the prompt warns against). Common in-aisle everyday errand.
items.how: Add a keyless deterministic unit-price tool: parse (qty, unit, price) pairs, convert each to a common base (reuse units-convert), compute price-per-base-unit, declare the cheaper. Pure, offline-testable. New TOOLS[] entry + dispatch + prompt + HELP + sorted tool-list test.

items.title: reminder grabs an HH:MM from the TASK text, fires at the wrong hour
items.why: The 24-hour branch (at24) runs before am/pm and its 'at' is optional, so 'remind me at 9am to submit the 10:30 report' grabs the FIRST bare HH:MM anywhere (10:30 inside the task) ahead of the explicit 'at 9am' -> fires 10:30, stores a mangled task. User is told a next-fire time but it lands at the wrong hour. Reminders are the highest-trust feature; wrong-time is worse than a loud fail.
items.how: Require the at24 colon-time to be anchored ('at'/'tomorrow' immediately before it), OR only take at24 when the am/pm branch found no time. Prefer: if an explicit am/pm time exists anywhere, it wins over a bare colon-time in the body. Offline test: 'at 9am to submit the 10:30 report' fires 09:00, task='submit the 10:30 report'.

items.title: unit_price breaks on a thousands-separated price ("$1,299 for 3")
items.why: parseUnitPrice splits on s*[;,]s* BEFORE per-option comma-stripping, so '$1,299 for 3 vs $1,499 for 4' splits into '$1'/'299 for 3' -> both unparseable -> null -> the model falls back to mental math (the silently-wrong arithmetic the tool exists to prevent). Bulk/electronics compares routinely have 4-digit prices. Regression in the just-shipped unit_price.
items.how: Strip in-number thousands commas (comma between digits) BEFORE the or/vs/comma separator split in parseUnitPrice. Offline test: '$1,299 for 3 vs $1,499 for 4' parses to 2 options.

items.title: "remind me to check on mom" runs a browser errand instead of echoing
items.why: FETCH_CUE_RE still includes 'check on' + 'check the', which dominate personal caretaking to-dos ('check on mom at 8pm', 'check on the baby every hour') — so the reminder is NOT reminder-only + at fire time runs a confused 20-40s browser agent/refusal instead of echoing the note. The block comment says the list was narrowed for exactly this (reminder-only-common-verb) but these two remain.
items.how: Drop 'check on' from FETCH_CUE_RE; keep 'check the <data-noun>' only when followed by a real lookup noun (weather/price/score/news/status), not a person. Offline test: 'check on mom' + 'check on the baby' -> reminderOnly true; 'check the weather' stays agent-path.

items.title: a watch reads "1.2M subscribers" as 1.2 (off by 6 orders of magnitude)
items.why: extractValue excludes bare m/t from the untagged magnitude branch (to avoid '3m ago'/'5t'), but a plain '1.2M subscribers' (no $ or %) collapses to 1.2 -> a 'below 50000'/'above 2000000' predicate fires/never-fires against a value off by 6+ orders, + the series records garbage. Same class as the fixed $60k bug, uncaught for non-currency counts (followers/subs/views/tokens).
items.how: Accept a magnitude suffix (k/m/b/t) when glued to the number AND followed by a word boundary/plural noun (not a bare standalone letter) even without a currency tag: '1.2M subscribers' -> 1200000, '3m ago' stays untouched. Offline test in alerts extractValue.

items.title: extractValue over-scales any number before a bare k/b word ("4 boxes"->4e9)
items.why: The untagged magnitude scan /(d+)s?(k|bn|b|thousand|million|billion|trillion)?/ excludes bare m/t (to avoid '3m ago') but LEFT bare k and b. So a non-currency count reply '4 boxes left' matches the 'b'illion suffix -> 4,000,000,000; '3 bedrooms'->3e9; '5 kids'/'3 km'/'2 kg'->x1000. A 'below 10'/'above N' predicate then false-fires/misses + recordPoint logs phantom multi-billion spikes. My count-magnitude fix added the count-noun path but didn't tighten the GENERAL branch's bare k/b. Broad silent-wrong across count/inventory/rental watches.
items.how: In the untagged branch require the k/b/etc suffix be followed by a word boundary NOT a letter (mirror the m/t exclusion): a bare 'b'/'k' immediately followed by a letter ('boxes','km','kids','kg') must NOT scale. Only 'k'/'b' at a true token end (or the explicit bn/billion/thousand words) scale. Keep the count-noun path ('900k downloads') working. Offline test: '4 boxes left'->4, '3 km'->3, '2 kg'->2, '900k downloads'->900000, '$60k'->60000.

items.title: a timer / short reminder is deferred hours by quiet-hours
items.why: The timer + relative-once branches return {kind:'once', dueMs:now+ms, reminderOnly:true} with NO clockTime flag, and schedule-runner only exempts isClockOnce from the quiet-hours defer. So with quiet hours on, 'timer for 20 minutes' at 11pm (or 'remind me in 30 min') is pushed to the window end (e.g. 7am) — the most common errand silently breaks by hours. Gated on RELAY_QUIET_START/END being set (off by default), so latent.
items.how: Exempt a SHORT-HORIZON once (timer, or a relative 'in N min/hours' due within the quiet window's start) from the quiet defer, mirroring the clock-once alarm exemption — the fire instant is deliberate + near-term. Offline test: a timer inside the quiet window fires at its time, not deferred.

items.title: no "text me if it rains tomorrow" weather-conditional alert
items.why: 'text me tomorrow morning if it's going to rain' / 'ping me if it drops below freezing tonight' — the most-wanted PROACTIVE weather errand — has no path; only a flaky agent-driven prose watch. get_weather (keyless open-meteo) + the alert engine's edge-triggered numeric + feedSource plumbing already exist. This is the flagship 'proactive assistant' promise new users test in minute one.
items.how: Add a weather-alert kind: parse 'if it rains/snows tomorrow', 'if it drops below X', 'if above X', 'if wind over X'; on each check fetch the forecast (hourly rain-timing already built) + evaluate the predicate edge-triggered (fire when it FIRST becomes true), reusing the alert seen-set/scheduler. Offline-testable with an injected forecast. New parse + a runner branch or a feedSource-style checker.

items.title: proactive pings are text-only — no one-tap Refresh/Snooze/Stop/Run-again buttons
items.why: Every alert/digest/reminder/recipe result is a dead-end requiring the user to compose a reply; callback_query is completely unwired (telegram.ts has only request_location). Retention lives on recurring touchpoints, and each is friction. Flagged by the audit as the single biggest cheap retention win, resurfacing repeatedly. task-suggest already computes the next action but delivers it as retype-it text.
items.how: Wire Telegram inline keyboards (reply_markup) + a callback_query handler + a small payload registry, and attach one-tap actions (Refresh/Run again/Snooze/Stop watching/Show more, pick-a-result) to proactive sends + suggestion prose. Offline-testable by feeding injected callback deltas through the handler. Bigger surface (channel + handler) — scope carefully.

items.title: multi-result pings dump a list — no one-tap pick
items.why: When a watch/errand returns several options (cheapest flights, new listings, restock sizes), the user gets a text wall and must retype to drill in. A one-tap pick button per result closes the loop the inline-tap-buttons plumbing now enables.
items.how: Extend the callback codec with a 'pick' op carrying a compact result index/id; attach a numbered button row to list-shaped proactive/errand replies; on tap, expand that result (details/link/next action). Reuse the callbacks.ts codec + handler routing already built.

items.title: button taps send a NEW message instead of updating the pinged one
items.why: Tapping Refresh/Snooze/Stop posts a fresh message, so a chat accretes duplicate cards. editMessageText/editMessageReplyMarkup would update the original ping in place (e.g. grey out Stop after stopping), which feels native and keeps the thread clean.
items.how: Add editMessageText/editMessageReplyMarkup to telegram.ts + the Channel; thread the tapped message_id (already parsed into callback) through the handler; for terminal actions (Stop) edit the original to a done state instead of sending a new line.

items.title: pick buttons only on inbound replies — proactive list pings still dump text
items.why: The inline-result-picker attaches 1/2/3 buttons to INBOUND agent answers, but a scheduled/alert list ping (a watchlist restock, new listings feed) still arrives as a text wall with no pick. Same value, other half of the surface.
items.how: In schedule-runner, parseResultList the proactive sendText; when it's a 2+ item list, attach pickButtons AND cache the items into the shared lastResult/pick store keyed by chat so a tap on a proactive ping resends the item. Reuse result-list.ts + the handler's pick routing already built.

items.title: onboarding is a text wall — no tap-to-try first errand
items.why: A new user texts hi, gets the START wall, must read + hand-type before anything happens; many bounce before first success.
items.how: Attach one-tap example buttons to START that RUN a canned keyless errand via the existing callback plumbing.

items.title: MemoryStore write failures are silent (no hedge, unlike every other store)
items.why: After a restart on a full/unwritable disk the bot has silently forgotten recent conversation, with no 'couldn't save' notice — the one store left un-hedged.
items.how: memory-store.ts persist() ignores atomicWriteJson's boolean; track lastWriteOk + expose lastSaveOk() like schedule/alert/recipe stores, and surface a one-time heads-up via the corrupt-notice path.

items.title: quiet hours bypassed for ALL alert types — feed/page/value watches buzz at 3am
items.why: A feed watch, page-diff, or plain price-change alert wakes the user at 3am even when the change persists and could wait until morning.
items.how: schedule-runner skips the quiet-defer for every alert: task; the exemption (an edge-triggered crossing could revert) only applies to predicate/weather alerts. Defer the SEND for feed/page/value-change alerts (change persists); keep predicate/weather exempt.

items.title: a noisy watch silently drops the user's plain daily briefing when the hourly cap is hit
items.why: A relied-upon 'every morning: weather + news' silently no-shows because a spammy alert filled the per-chat hourly send counter.
items.how: In schedule-runner give a plain daily/recipe the same defer-then-force grace as once/monthly/digest (graceEligible) so it isn't dropped over-cap; or don't count edge-triggered alert sends toward the cap that starves content.

items.title: sports is today-only — 'when do the Lakers play next' returns nothing
items.why: A very common casual sports ask ('next Arsenal game', 'when do the Lakers play next') gets today's score or 'not playing today', never the upcoming fixture — a high-frequency errand goes unanswered.
items.how: scores.ts already hits the keyless ESPN scoreboard which has scheduled/'pre' games; surface the next scheduled game (date/time/opponent) when there's no game today or the user asks 'next'. Keyless, extends an existing path.

items.title: a fresh inbound answer has no one-tap 'watch this / save this' button
items.why: Inline buttons only attach to PROACTIVE pings; a fresh answer gets at most a text save-nudge nobody acts on. One tap to turn any answer into a recurring watch/alert/saved recipe is the retention flywheel, and the button + alert/recipe backends already exist.
items.how: On a clean inbound text answer, attach a small keyboard (Watch this / Save / Daily) via the existing callbacks codec; a tap wires the alert/recipe the save-nudge currently only describes in prose. Reuse callbacks.ts + handler routing.

items.title: transit directions silently answered as a car ETA
items.why: 'how long downtown by subway/bus/train' returns an OSRM car ETA labeled 'drive' — a confidently wrong answer, violating the no-silent-wrong-answer principle.
items.how: directions.ts routeMode() maps transit->driving with no note; detect transit intent and either say so + hand back a Google Maps transit link, or label the estimate honestly as driving-only.

items.title: a 3-24h 'remind me in N hours' set at night is deferred to quiet-end, firing hours late
items.why: 'remind me in 4 hours' at 11pm lands at 7am (quiet-end) not 3am — a deliberate duration silently broken; isShortOnce only exempts onces due within 3h.
items.how: schedule-runner: a relative once (no clockTime) of ANY horizon names a deliberate instant — exempt it from the quiet-hours defer (or raise the short-once window), like a clock-time alarm; a recurring daily/digest still defers.

items.title: a digest/recipe goes permanently silent when its member recipes are deleted
items.why: The relied-upon morning briefing just stops arriving with zero explanation when a member recipe is forgotten; the runner completes+advances silently on a null compose.
items.how: When digestRun/recipeResolveTask returns null (members gone), send a one-time 'your <name> briefing has no content left — its recipes were removed' notice instead of silently advancing forever.

items.title: a bare 'ok'/'stop' silently deletes an active sticky nag
items.why: A standing 'nag me to take meds until done' sticky was deleted by an unrelated 'ok'/'got it' reply hours after it last pinged — the highest-trust safety-net reminder destroyed by a filler word.
items.how: Gate the bare-ack sticky-stop on a RECENTLY-fired (or not-yet-fired) sticky.

items.title: flight status lookup ('is AA100 on time / what gate')
items.why: A very common assistant errand — 'is AA100 delayed / what gate / when does it land' — dead-ends: track_package only recognizes UPS/FedEx/USPS/DHL parcel numbers, and a flight number falls to a flaky web_search.
items.how: anvil (real Chrome) can scrape Google's flight-status card the same way track_package scrapes carrier pages; add a flight-number detector + a get_flight backend that reads the status/gate/times. Keyless, high-frequency, high-stakes.

items.title: a watch reading error/degraded replies silently dies (no receipt)
items.why: A watch whose source keeps returning error-shaped/degraded/empty reads never notifies AND never throws, so the failed-watch receipt (thrown-only) never fires — user thinks it's armed for weeks while dead.
items.how: Flag genuine soft-fails from checkAlert; count a per-watch consecutive soft-fail streak in the runner; send the failed-watch receipt after N.

items.title: background errand delivered twice after a crash (no delivered-dedup)
items.why: If Relay crashes after sending a background-errand result but before bgErrandDone clears the record, startup recovery re-runs the whole errand and texts a second (possibly different) unprompted answer.
items.how: Mirror the once-schedule delivered flag: mark the errand delivered before the finally-clear, and skip replay of a delivered errand on startup recovery (planErrandReplay).

items.title: in_stock watch never fires when the buy CTA sits in cross-sell framing
items.why: 'alert me when back in stock' stays silent even after buyable, on pages whose only availability signal is an Add-to-cart CTA surrounded by 'you may also like' framing — conditionHolds returns null indefinitely.
items.how: In conditionHolds in_stock: when CTA_RE matches but CROSS_SELL_RE also matches, don't hold null forever — fall back to a positive on a primary/above-the-fold CTA, or after K ambiguous checks treat a persistent CTA as in-stock.

items.title: saved named places (home/work/gym) — one location only today
items.why: 'directions to work', 'weather at the gym', 'coffee near home' re-ask the city each time; profile stores exactly ONE location.
items.how: A per-chat place-alias store (name -> coords/label); resolve an alias in directions/find_nearby/weather before geocoding. Sharpens every location errand + is the prerequisite for geofencing.

items.title: failed proactive send silently swallows a crossing / drops a reminder
items.why: sendMessage catches all errors + resolves void, so the runner's 'commit baseline / complete only after a successful send' guards were dead code — a 429/network/blocked send advanced the alert baseline anyway (crossing lost forever) and completed a once (reminder dropped).
items.how: sendMessage returns a delivered-boolean; the runner skips commit/complete + throws on a false return so it re-fires.

items.title: feed + watchlist alerts never emit softFail, so a dead one dies dark
