items.why: The silent-watch-death receipt only fires on softFail, which alert-runner sets on the value/page/weather paths but NOT the watchlist branch nor the two feed branches — a persistently-dead RSS/Reddit/HN feed or stock-basket watch looks armed forever with no receipt.
items.how: Return softFail:true from the feedSource-empty / watchlist-all-members-failed paths in alert-runner (mirror the single-value degraded/error-reply guards) so the runner's soft-fail streak + receipt covers them too.

items.title: quick 'who/what is X' facts are slow + unreliable (no keyless summary tool)
items.why: 'who is the CEO of OpenAI'/'how tall is Everest'/'what is a Roth IRA' waits 10-30s on web_search->scrape->summarize (sometimes wrong page), when a keyless Wikipedia REST summary answers in ~200ms with a citation. The most common text-a-bot first errand is the slowest path.
items.how: A get_fact tool hitting en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/summary/<title> (keyless GET, same fast-path shape as define/get_time); parse title/extract/url, format + cite. Fall back to web_search on a miss/disambiguation.

items.title: tabular results can't be exported ('send that as a spreadsheet')
items.why: to-csv.ts (rowsToCsv) is already built but wired to NO tool; a compare/extract/watchlist/list result is lost the moment the chat scrolls.
items.how: Wire a to_csv tool (or an 'as a CSV' modifier on compare/extract) that turns rows into a .csv sent via the existing sendDocument path. Reuse rowsToCsv.

items.title: an over-cap sticky nag silently retires early (budget burned by an unsent ping)
items.why: A 'nag me to take my meds every 15 min until done' sticky is kind:interval (not graceEligible), so a busy/capped hour dropped it via safeComplete(s) with the default fired:true — incrementing stickyFired toward stickyMax for a ping that never sent, silently retiring the safety-net.
items.how: Drop the over-cap occurrence with fired:false so the anti-nag budget isn't burned by an unsent ping (mirror the send-fail-burns-budget guard).

items.title: benign browse clicks refused by the destructive-action guard
items.why: DANGEROUS_ACTION_RE matches bare nouns order|book|send|reset|remove|close|confirm against label+selector, so legit navigation ('Order status', 'Bookings', a .remove-filter selector) dead-ends a multi-step browse with 'that looks destructive' — the core browse differentiator silently stalls.
items.how: Require committing-verb CONTEXT ('place order', 'confirm booking', 'delete account') rather than the bare noun; keep the guard strict on genuine commit phrasing.

items.title: a plain 'watch X: price of Y' fires on every check, all hours
items.why: A no-threshold change-watch on a volatile value (BTC/stock/temp) is level-triggered (changed() true on any delta>0), and value alerts skip BOTH the anti-spam cap AND quiet hours — so the headline watch feature can spam the user overnight with no way to know they needed a threshold.
items.how: Give a no-threshold change alert a minimum re-notify interval (e.g. once/6h unless it crosses a magnitude), OR treat a plain change-watch as quiet-deferrable so it batches to morning.

items.title: a permanently-erroring watchlist member never alerts + never warns
items.why: A watchlist member whose source errors EVERY tick (bad ticker, login wall) is dropped via looksLikeErrorReply->continue before it's seeded, so its last stays undefined + it's excluded from changedLines forever; other readable members keep anyReadable true, so no per-member failed-watch receipt ever fires — the user believes all N items are tracked.
items.how: Track per-member consecutive-fail streaks in the watchlist branch + surface a receipt naming the persistently-dead member (the soft-fail streak currently only covers an ALL-dead basket).

items.title: price checks give a bare number, not a 'good deal?' verdict from history
items.why: chart.ts already draws a series + alerts store lastValue, but a price check/watch answers with just the number — no 'lowest in 60 days, buy' verdict, the stickiest recurring reason to re-check.
items.how: Persist a per-item price history + compute a verdict string (lowest/highest/median over N days) appended to a price answer + watch ping. Reuse the alert series machinery.

items.title: calorie/macro lookup ('calories in a banana') has no tool -> guessed
items.why: 'how many calories in 2 eggs' / 'carbs in a Big Mac' falls to a slow web_search with conflicting numbers or the model silently invents figures — photo-intent.ts even matches calories|carbs|nutrition but nothing backs it. A daily health errand answered unreliably.
items.how: A get_nutrition tool: keyless Open Food Facts (branded items by name/barcode) + a small static table or USDA FoodData DEMO_KEY for whole foods; parse kcal/protein/carbs/fat, format, cite. Mirror meals.ts' food-data pattern. Say 'I'm not sure' on a miss rather than inventing.

items.title: 'where can I stream X' / movie rating has no tool -> cold web_search
items.why: 'is Dune 2 any good' / 'where can I watch Oppenheimer' is a top evening errand that falls to a flaky logged-out scrape floating a number with no source or streaming answer.
items.how: anvil drives a JustWatch (or Google) title page for streaming availability + a rating; reuse the browse/extract tools. Or a keyless-ish source if one exists. Report rating + where-to-stream + a link, honest on a miss.

items.title: 'watch btc: below 50k' silently becomes a fire-on-every-wiggle change-watch
items.why: The below/above/by operand regex accepted only plain digits (no k/m/bn suffix, nothing trailing), so '50k'/'1.2M'/'50,000 usd' — the dominant way people write levels — failed to parse the condition and fell through to a plain change-watch that pings on every delta, never on the crossing asked for; confirmation never revealed the threshold was dropped.
items.how: Scale a trailing magnitude suffix + tolerate a currency word in the operand grammar, mirroring extractValue on the value side; shared parseOperand.

items.title: a failed inbound reply is invisible + memory records it as delivered
items.why: sendMessage returns a delivered-boolean the PROACTIVE runner gates on, but the inbound handler ignores it — a 429/network/one-chunk failure means the user gets nothing/truncated with no notice, and the assistant turn is still written to memory as answered (next turn's context claims an answer never seen).
items.how: Check sendMessage's return on the inbound path; on false, don't write the assistant turn to memory as delivered (or note the miss) + optionally retry once — mirror the proactive commit-gating already built.

items.title: the flagship '☀️ Weather' tap-to-try asks 'which city?' instead of answering
items.why: The onboarding tap-to-try row exists to manufacture a first win, but a cold user (no saved location) taps the top button and gets 'What city are you in?' — the one dead-end in an otherwise instant onboarding.
items.how: Change the TRY_EXAMPLES weather entry to a city-bearing example ('weather in New York') or reorder a no-location example first, so the first tap always lands an answer.

items.title: 'days until' is one-shot — no saved countdown with milestone pings
items.why: datecalc computes a difference on demand; nothing persists a countdown or pings at milestones. Countdowns (trips/birthdays/deadlines) are emotionally sticky + every proactive ping is a re-engagement touch.
items.how: A tiny countdown store + a scheduler-backed item ('countdown to my flight Dec 20') that fires milestone pings (1 week, tomorrow); reuse schedule.ts + datecalc + safe-store.

items.title: no personal quick-log tracker ('log weight 182', 'spent $14 lunch') + trends
items.why: Notes stores facts, alerts watch external values — nothing lets a user log their OWN tagged data points + ask 'show my weight this month' / 'how much did I spend on food'. The single strongest daily-habit retention primitive Relay lacks; Instinct's moat is 'the assistant that remembers your life'.
items.how: A tagged append-only store (tag -> [{t,v}]) + parse 'log <tag> <value>' + a 'show/how much <tag>' aggregator (sum/avg/latest/trend). Reuse chart.ts (line chart), summarizeSeries, to-csv, safe-store. Keyless.

items.title: reminders aren't person-anchored ('follow up with Sarah in 3 days')
items.why: Reminders exist but aren't tied to a PERSON, and contacts.ts is a passive lookup. 'nudge me to reply to my landlord' / 'follow up with Sarah Fri' should fire AND pull that contact's details + offer a tap-to-draft (compose) in the same ping — a lightweight personal-CRM loop, the 'assistant that has your back' behavior.
items.how: Parse 'follow up with <contact> <when>' -> a reminder-once whose task references the contact; on fire, resolve the saved contact + append their email/phone + a compose deep-link. Reuse schedule + contacts + compose.

items.title: an immediate alert check (define/edit/refresh) eats the crossing if its ping fails to send
items.why: The four inbound run-now sites (define, edit, watch-that, refresh) did 'await sendMessage(...); commit()' unconditionally; sendMessage returns false on a failed send (doesn't throw), so a 429/network drop advanced the baseline anyway — the crossing is eaten + the watch looks armed but won't re-fire until it crosses again.
items.how: Gate each message-path commit on (await sendMessage(...)) !== false, mirroring the scheduler's send-gated commit.

items.title: photo/doc reply memory write isn't gated on delivery
items.why: The text path was fixed (inbound-send-fail-swallowed) but the photo/document/photo-to-action branches call memorySet unconditionally after the send — a failed image/PDF answer is still recorded as delivered, so the next message is read as a follow-up to an answer the user never saw.
items.how: Gate the media-branch memorySet on the sendPhoto/sendDocument result (=== false skip), mirroring the text path.

items.title: a scheduled chained recipe that stops early is delivered as if complete
items.why: The inbound /run path flags stoppedEarly/stepsDone, but the scheduled path's runChain dep returns Promise<string> — a chain halted at an if-gate or degraded step is pushed as a normal complete-looking briefing every period, no '⚠️ couldn't finish'.
items.how: Change the scheduler's runChain dep to return the structured { final, stoppedEarly, stepsDone } the inbound path consumes + prefix a partial-answer banner on a proactive fire.

items.title: the recurring-automation engine is under-adopted (no tap-to-install)
items.why: Recipes/digests/alerts/watchlists are deep but activation needs 'save X:'/'digest morning: ...' syntax users never discover; onboarding tap-to-try only fires ONE-SHOT errands. Retention is gated on setting up >=1 recurring automation.
items.how: An /automations (or onboarding) row of ~10 curated recurring automations ('Daily weather + top news', 'Watch a product price', 'Job feed', 'Morning briefing') that a tap installs into the existing recipe/alert/digest stores — a new 'install' callback op reusing callbacks.ts + a static list like TRY_EXAMPLES.

items.title: a dead digest source sends a reassuring 'temporary blip' note forever
items.why: digest-runner returns an all-failed note as a normal string; the runner sends it + completes ok:true, so the softFail/fail-streak machinery never engages. A genuinely dead digest (bad recipe, permanently blocked URL) keeps sending 'I couldn't put your briefing together this time, I'll try next run' every morning with no escalation, and if THAT send fails it's silently lost.
items.how: Have digest-runner signal all-failed as a soft-fail (like watches) so the runner streaks it + sends a failed-watch-style receipt after N ('your <name> briefing has failed K days — check its recipes'); gate the note send on delivery.

items.title: No-threshold numeric watch pings on any nonzero move
items.why: changed() returned delta>0 with no threshold; a bare 'watch bitcoin price' fires on every sub-cent tick, and alerts skip anti-spam + quiet hours -> firehose trains the user to mute the bot.
items.how: Relative deadband (default 0.5%, env RELAY_ALERT_DEADBAND_PCT) for no-threshold numeric compares; move off zero always fires; explicit threshold still wins; text-diff path unchanged.

items.title: Plain greeting skips the START menu, burns a cold agent turn
items.why: START/onboarding buttons only fire on /start; 'hi'/'hello'/'what can you do' route straight to the agent, so most users never see the tap-to-try examples on their real first message.
items.how: Detect a bare greeting/help-ask in the handler (before the agent dispatch) and reply with the START menu + try-buttons instead of a cold agent run.

items.title: Corrupt-store notice consumed even if its send fails
items.why: handler drains corruptNotice() on read but sends best-effort with .catch(()=>{}); a single failed send permanently loses the only signal that saved reminders/alerts/recipes vanished.
items.how: Gate the drain on delivery: only clear the pending corrupt-notice once the send resolves truthy (mirror the send-never-throws-dead-commit-guard pattern), else re-surface next inbound.

items.title: Slow send past the fire timeout double-pings a reminder
items.why: fireOne guards every side-effect with isCancelled() EXCEPT after await deps.send(...); a send that outlasts the 90s per-fire timeout is delivered once, then the timeout's catch retries the once -> 'take your meds' twice.
items.how: Re-check isCancelled() immediately after the send resolves; if the fire already timed out, skip complete()/recordSend so the late-landing send isn't also retried. Mirror the existing pre-send isCancelled guards.

items.title: 6k-char page truncation answered from the top slice as fact
items.why: truncateForModel caps a fetched page at ~6000 chars + appends a hedge marker, but nothing forces the model to heed it, so a long listing/article yields a confident partial answer with an authoritative 'Source:' line while a price/score lower down is missed.
items.how: Strengthen the truncation marker into an explicit instruction the model must surface ('I only saw the top of this page') OR chunk-and-scan when the answer isn't in the first slice; at minimum tag the reply as partial so it isn't shown as complete.

items.title: Alert extractValue mis-picks the number on a multi-figure reply
items.why: extractValue is a positional heuristic; a watch reply like 'AAPL $230, up 2%, volume 50M' can track 2 or 50 instead of 230, so the user gets a false 'changed' ping, a missed crossing, or a receipt showing the wrong figures — corrupting the core watch-and-notify promise.
items.how: Bias extractValue toward the figure that matches the alert's own units/currency + the tracked task text (prefer a $-prefixed or task-keyword-adjacent number over a bare % / volume); add tests for multi-figure replies.

items.title: Reminders fire in the wrong timezone until a manual UTC offset is set
items.why: 'remind me at 7am' fires at the server's zone (e.g. 3am) until the user knows to append 'UTC-5' to /setlocation; a silently-wrong reminder on day one destroys trust and the code itself flags the 3am surprise.
items.how: Infer the tz offset from the user's saved city/location (a keyless offline city->tz table or the existing geo context) so a set location implies its timezone; keep the explicit UTC-n override as a manual win.

items.title: A long-lived recurring reminder drifts an hour across a DST boundary
items.why: A daily/weekly stores a fixed offsetMin at creation; when the clock crosses a DST boundary the stored offset is now an hour wrong, so a '7am' daily fires at 6am (or 8am) for the rest of the season until re-set. The new city->IANA zone map lets the fire recompute the correct offset per occurrence.
items.how: Store the IANA zone (not just offsetMin) on a schedule when inferred; in nextDaily/Weekly/Monthly recompute the offset via offsetForZoneAt(zone, targetMs) so each occurrence lands at the right wall-clock hour regardless of DST. Keep offsetMin as the fallback when no zone is known.

items.title: First weather/near-me errand dead-ends to setup instead of a one-tap share
items.why: A brand-new user's 'weather?'/'coffee near me' asks them to run /setlocation or share a pin from a buried tip, instead of offering an inline one-tap 'share location' button — a first-touch errand that bounces to setup reads as broken.
items.how: On a needsLocationContext ask with no saved location/coords, reply with a Telegram request_location keyboard button (one tap sends the pin, already handled by the location-pin path) alongside the 'or tell me your city' text.

items.title: World-clock/get_time was standard-time-only (hour off in DST)
items.why: runWorldClock used fixed standard offsets and appended 'may be an hour off during daylight-saving' to EVERY answer, so 'time in London' in summer was wrong (GMT not BST) and even correct answers carried a trust-eroding disclaimer.
items.how: resolveZone(text, atMs) resolves a city/region via its IANA zone (offsetForZoneAt) for the DST-correct offset at the query instant; a typed abbreviation (PST/EST) stays as-is; the disclaimer shows only when an offset is standard-only. Tool descriptions updated.

items.title: Verify sunrise/sunset + any other tz-derived tool for the same DST gap
items.why: get_time was standard-time-only; suntimes.ts + datecalc.ts + the agent's current-datetime line may share the same fixed-offset assumption and be an hour off in DST months for a named city.
items.how: Audit suntimes/datecalc/status for CITY_TZ/fixed-offset use; route city-derived times through offsetForZoneAt(zone, atMs) like worldclock now does; add DST tests.

items.title: 'save this' link -> summarize + recall over saved pages
items.why: A satisfied user has no way to build a personal corpus; 'save this <link>' + later 'what did I save about X' turns normal use into a knowledge base + switching-cost moat (parked audit-C finding).
items.how: On 'save this <url>' scrape+summarize via the existing tools, store {url,summary,tags,t} in a notes-style store; 'what did I save about X' does full-text recall. Reuse notes.ts/lists.ts + scrape.

items.title: Fold saved reading list into a digest / weekly recap
items.why: read-it-later now stores summarized pages, but they're only pulled on explicit recall; a satisfied user would value 'my weekly reading recap' or a digest member that surfaces what they saved but haven't revisited — deepens the retention hook.
items.how: Add a digest-member/recipe source that lists recent saved pages (or unread-since-saved), reusing SavedStore.search + the existing digest-runner; optional 'mark read' via a callback.

items.title: Let the agent itself save a page it just found
items.why: A user who says 'find me a good pasta recipe and save it' can't — save is only a top-level command; the agent has no save_page tool, so a found-then-save flow needs two manual turns.
items.how: Add a save_page(url,title?,summary?) agent tool that writes to SavedStore (same store as the command path), so the agent can capture a result it just produced; guard against saving junk (require a real URL).

items.title: Nudge saved pages the user never revisited
items.why: the reading-list recap surfaces recent saves but doesn't track whether the user actually re-opened one, so a saved-and-forgotten page never gets a second nudge — the read-it-later value leaks.
items.how: Record a lastRecalledAt when a page appears in a recall/recap; add a 'saved but not revisited in N days' view + an optional weekly 'still want to read these?' proactive nudge, reusing SavedStore + the scheduler.

items.title: Tell the user when a save updated vs added a duplicate link
items.why: re-saving the same URL silently updates in place; the agent save_page path doesn't distinguish add vs update in its confirmation, so a user re-saving a link isn't told it was already there.
items.how: Thread the SavedStore dup flag through the agent save_page tool result (the command path already says Updated/Saved) so the agent's confirmation matches.

items.title: Proactively ping stale-unread saves once a week
items.why: 'what haven't I read' now works on demand + unread state is tracked, but a forgotten save still only resurfaces if the user thinks to ask; a gentle weekly proactive nudge would actually close the loop.
items.how: A scheduled reminder-style job (opt-in, reuse scheduler) that fires formatUnreadNudge(saved.unread(...)) once a week per chat if there are stale-unread pages, gated on the anti-spam cap + quiet hours + delivery like other proactive sends; skip silently when none.

items.title: Unit-price compare missed the connector-less shelf phrasing
items.why: parseOption required a connector (for/at/@) between qty+unit and price, so '12 rolls $6 vs 8 rolls $4.50' — a natural grocery/shelf phrasing — returned null and dead-ended to the agent's forbidden mental math (silently-wrong per-unit comparison).
items.how: Added a Form A2 in parseOption for '<qty><unit> $<price>', requiring the price to be $-prefixed so an ambiguous '12 rolls 6' (is 6 a price or a 2nd qty?) still needs an explicit connector.

items.title: Unit-price: verify 3+ options + the % savings wording
items.why: the comparator handles N options but the phrasing/tests focus on 2; a 3-way compare's 'better buy (X% cheaper)' line compares only to the runner-up, which may read oddly with 3+.
items.how: Add 3-way tests; consider phrasing the savings vs the most-expensive or naming rank, so a 3-option compare reads clearly.

items.title: Watch command split on a URL-scheme colon, making a garbage alert
items.why: parseAlertCommand split name:task on the FIRST colon, so 'watch this page https://ex.com for changes' split at 'https:' -> a garbage alert named 'this page https' watching '//ex.com for changes' instead of a page-diff watch (or falling through).
items.how: Added a (?!//) guard to the separator colon so a URL-scheme colon isn't treated as the name:task boundary; a real 'name: <url>' (colon + space) still splits.

items.title: Single-slot recipe run with a name=value arg keeps the literal 'name='
items.why: applySlots fills a SINGLE slot with the whole arg string verbatim, so '/run greet name=Sam' on 'hi {name}' yields 'hi name=Sam' instead of 'hi Sam' — a user who mirrors the multi-slot name=value form gets the literal pair.
items.how: In the single-slot branch, if the arg is a lone 'slotname=value' matching the slot, use just the value; else keep the whole-string fill (a bare 'oat milk' still works).

items.title: Dangerous-action guard missed 'Send $50 to John' + 'empty trash'
items.why: isDangerousAction caught 'send money' by the word 'money' but NOT a currency AMOUNT ('Send $50 to John', 'transfer £200', 'pay 100 usd', 'Venmo $20') — a real money-movement commit the agent could click autonomously — and 'empty trash'/'clear my cart' (bulk-destructive) also passed. A safety false-negative on the exact irreversible actions the guard exists to block.
items.how: Added CONTEXTUAL_RE branches: send/transfer/wire/pay/venmo/zelle/paypal + a $/€/£ or number+currency-word amount, and empty|clear (the) trash/bin/cart/basket/inbox. Verified no overblock of send search / send email / send the link / clear filters / empty state.

items.title: Sweep the dangerous-action guard for more money/destroy verbs
items.why: the send-amount fix covers the common payment phrasings, but adjacent commits may still slip: 'apply for', 'accept offer', 'agree and continue', 'delete all', 'unfriend/block', 'cash out', a bare 'send' to a @handle.
items.how: Adversarially probe isDangerousAction with a list of real commit/destroy button labels; add the misses to CONTEXTUAL_RE, re-verifying benign navigation isn't overblocked (keep the two-tier discipline).

items.title: Confirm isDangerousAction actually gates the click/type dispatch at runtime
items.why: the guard's REGEX is now well-tested, but the loop's value depends on the agent's click/type/submit dispatch actually calling isDangerousAction on the target text + refusing — a wiring regression would silently disarm it with all unit tests still green.
items.how: Trace the click/type tool dispatch in agent.ts; add an integration test that a scripted 'click Pay now' is refused (not dispatched to the backend) and a 'click Read more' proceeds, so the gate is proven wired, not just the regex.

items.title: Audit memory/notes/store eviction + persistence-failure UX for silent data loss
items.why: several stores cap per-chat + drop oldest; a silent eviction of the earliest (often most important) item, or a persist failure not surfaced, reads as 'the bot forgot' — worth a sweep for any store that evicts/fails without telling the user (notes already warns; others may not).
items.how: Probe NotesStore/SavedStore/ListStore/ContactStore/PlacesStore add() at the cap + lastSaveOk() paths; ensure eviction returns what was dropped + the handler surfaces it, and a failed persist hedges the confirmation. Fix any that silently lose.

items.title: Audit digest/recipe/alert member caps for the same silent-drop class
items.why: lists had a silent over-cap drop; a digest caps members (maxMembers/slice), a watchlist caps sub-watches (MAX_WATCHLIST_MEMBERS slice), a recipe chain may cap steps — each may silently drop the tail without telling the user, the same trust bug just fixed for lists.
items.how: Probe DigestStore.add member slice, AlertStore watchlist member slice, and any recipe/chain step cap; where the definition exceeds the cap, surface 'kept the first N, dropped X' instead of a silent slice.

items.title: Chain recipe silently truncates past MAX_CHAIN_STEPS (6)
items.why: parseChainSteps slices at 6 steps with no signal, so a 'a >> b >> ... >> h' recipe silently drops steps 7+; a power user building a long workflow loses the tail without knowing (same class as the digest/watchlist/list caps just fixed, lower frequency).
items.how: Surface the dropped step count when a chain definition exceeds MAX_CHAIN_STEPS (on save/define), e.g. 'kept the first 6 steps, dropped 2' — reusing the cap-report pattern.

items.title: 'follow news.ycombinator.com' silently never fired (HN URL parsed as dead RSS)
items.why: resolveFeedSource fell the HN homepage URL through to the bare-URL RSS branch, which fetched + RSS-parsed HN's HTML homepage (no feed there) — so a 'follow news.ycombinator.com' watch saw zero items forever, a silently-dead subscription.
items.how: Map the HN host (news.ycombinator.com / bare ycombinator.com, not other subdomains or /item,/user permalinks) to the keyless Algolia front-page feed before the bare-URL branch — same feed as the 'HN' keyword.

items.title: Sweep resolveFeedSource for other paste-a-URL feeds that dead-parse
items.why: HN's homepage URL dead-parsed; other common paste targets (a subreddit URL variant, a bare twitter/x handle, a YouTube @handle URL which needs a channel-id lookup) may also fall to the bare-URL RSS branch + silently never fire.
items.how: Probe resolveFeedSource with the URLs users actually paste; for ones with no keyless feed (YT @handle needs a lookup), return null so the caller falls back to the agent feed-watch instead of a dead RSS parse.

items.title: Tell users what they can follow (reddit/HN/YouTube-channel/GitHub/RSS)
items.why: follow now supports r/x, HN, YouTube /channel, GitHub releases, Reddit user, and any RSS URL — but HELP/START don't enumerate them, so a user won't discover 'follow github.com/owner/repo' or that a YouTube @handle needs the channel URL.
items.how: Add a follow-examples line to HELP + the START menu listing the supported source shapes + the YouTube channel-URL caveat.

items.title: 'days until Christmas' countdown labeled 'it' instead of the holiday
items.why: parseCountdown peels the trailing date phrase off the label; for a bare-holiday countdown ('days until Christmas') the holiday IS the whole phrase, so the label came out empty -> 'it', and the pings/confirmation read 'it is N days away' instead of naming the holiday.
items.how: When the label is empty but the date phrase is a NAME (alphabetic, not a numeric/ISO date), use that phrase as the label. Christmas/Halloween/new year/thanksgiving now label correctly; a bare ISO date still falls back to 'it'.

items.title: Retire buttons on other terminal taps (snooze, digest/recipe gone)
items.why: Stop now strips the tapped ping's buttons; other end-states leave a stale card — a Snoozed watch still shows a live Refresh, and a Run-again on a since-deleted digest/recipe keeps offering the button. editReplyMarkup is already wired, so extending it is cheap.
items.how: On snooze, swap the keyboard to a single 'Resume' (or strip Refresh); when digestRun/recipeRunByName returns null (gone), strip the tapped ping's buttons via editReplyMarkup(messageId) like Stop does.

items.title: Run a real anvil e2e pass once the browser is up (verify call-tested path)
items.why: Every recent change is unit-verified offline (anvil DOWN for many runs); the data-source + scrape/click paths have never been call-tested in this streak, so a live regression could hide behind green units.
items.how: When ctx_execute shows anvil localhost:3000/v1/live = 200, drive one real errand end-to-end via the console channel (e.g. a scrape + a get_weather) + assert a coherent reply; report call-tested:true. Owner-gated only in that it needs anvil started.

items.title: 'spent $1,250 on rent' silently failed to log (thousands comma)
items.why: parseLogCommand's amount pattern was \d+(\.\d+)? — no thousands comma — so a rent/salary/bill log with a comma ('spent $1,250 on rent', 'log salary 5,000') returned null and nothing was recorded, while the user thought it logged. A comma is exactly where big-ticket expenses appear.
items.how: Accept a thousands-separated NUM in both the money + generic branches, strip commas before parseFloat. Also allowed an optional leading 'I ' ('I spent $1,250 on rent') — a natural phrasing that also failed. Guarded so 'independent 5 on x' doesn't false-match the 'i' prefix.

items.title: 'day after tomorrow' + 'next <weekday>' resolved to the wrong forecast day
items.why: resolveWhen picked the wrong day for two common phrasings: 'day after tomorrow' matched the \btomorrow\b branch -> [1] (a day early), and 'next friday' only bumped +7 when it collided with today, so mid-week it returned THIS Friday not next week's. A weather answer for the wrong day reads as confidently correct.
items.how: Check 'day after tomorrow' (+2) BEFORE the tomorrow branch; make 'next <weekday>' always add a week past the soonest occurrence (not only on a today-collision). Both guarded by maxDays / handled out-of-window by formatWeatherWhen's 'beyond my N-day forecast' note.

items.title: Long calendar events produced an unfoldable .ics that strict apps reject
items.why: buildIcs emitted content lines unbounded, but RFC-5545 caps a line at 75 octets; a long SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION/LOCATION (e.g. 'add this event with its details to my calendar') made a 200-char line that Apple Calendar + some Outlook importers reject or truncate — the add-to-calendar artifact silently failed to import.
items.how: Added foldIcsLine: fold each content line at 75 UTF-8 octets with a leading-space continuation (measured by byte, iterating code points so a multi-byte char isn't split), applied to every line in buildIcs. Reversible (unfold recovers the value); short lines untouched.

items.title: 'where's UA83' / 'track BA2490' weren't detected as flight asks
items.why: detectFlight required a flight cue word (flight/land/gate/status/...) but 'where('s)' and 'track(ing)' — the two most natural flight-status phrasings — weren't cues, so 'where's UA83' and 'track BA2490' fell through to a flaky web_search instead of the keyless flight lookup.
items.how: Added where('s)/where is + track(ing) to the cue list. A parcel tracking number (1Z...) can't match FLIGHT_RE's 2-char+<=4-digit shape, so 'track' with a flight-shaped token is a flight; a cue with no such token still returns null.

items.title: 'days until my birthday on <date>' fell to a slow agent guess
items.why: runDateCalc's days-until branch passed the whole tail to parseDate, so a LABELED date ('my birthday on 2025-06-20', 'the deadline is July 4', 'my trip on X') failed to parse -> null -> the question fell through to a slow, non-deterministic agent run for math the tool should nail instantly.
items.how: When the whole phrase doesn't parse, peel a trailing date token (up to 4 words, stripping a leading on/is/for/by/the) and parse that, dropping the label. Plain 'days until Christmas' + bare-date + no-date->null all unchanged.

items.title: 'convert 100 kg to lbs please' failed — 'please' glued to the target unit
items.why: parseUnitConvert didn't strip a trailing politeness word/punctuation, so 'to lbs please' parsed to target unit 'lbs please' -> unknown unit -> the conversion returned null and a common polite phrasing silently failed (fell to a slow agent guess).
items.how: Strip a trailing please/thanks/thx/pls + trailing ?.! before matching (alongside the existing leading-'convert' strip). Regressions (180C to F, 5ft11 to cm, cross-dim null) unchanged.

items.title: 'remind me to call mom at 5pm please' stored the task as 'call mom please'
items.why: cleanTask didn't drop a trailing courtesy word, so 'please'/'pls' got baked into the stored reminder/recipe task — the reminder re-pinged '⏰ Reminder: call mom please' forever, and a recipe/daily ran 'send me the weather thanks' through the agent verbatim.
items.how: In cleanTask (the single task chokepoint for every schedule kind), strip a TRAILING please/pls/plz only — NOT 'thanks' (can be the task, 'say thanks') and NOT a mid-task 'please' ('say please to grandma'). Only when task text precedes it.

items.title: Trailing 'please'/'thanks' polluted stored notes, follows, and saved places
items.why: Same courtesy-tail bug as datecalc/unit-convert/schedule, in 3 more verbatim-storing parsers: parseRemember stored 'I'm vegetarian please' (recited forever), parseFollowCommand targeted 'r/programming please' / made a garbage 'HN thanks' feed, parseSavePlace stored 'Gold's on Main please' (breaks near-me geocoding).
items.how: Extracted a shared stripTrailingCourtesy(s,{onlyPlease?}) helper (src/lib/text-clean.ts) — strips a trailing please/pls/plz(/thanks) only when value text precedes it, keeps a mid-value or whole-value word. Applied in notes/feeds/places; refactored schedule.cleanTask to use it (onlyPlease=true, keeps 'say thanks'). DRY across the class.

items.title: Trailing courtesy poisoned watch tasks + targeted the wrong list
items.why: Two more verbatim-storing parsers had the courtesy-tail bug: parseAlertCommand watched 'price of bitcoin please' (poisons value extraction) + made a garbage watchlist member 'eth price thanks'; parseListCommand read 'add milk to my grocery list please' as the list name 'grocery list please' — a wrong/new list, so the item vanished from the real one.
items.how: Applied the shared stripTrailingCourtesy: on parseAlertCommand's task (before then/weather/watchlist/threshold parsing, so a member's tail is dropped before the ';' split) and at parseListCommand's input top (item sits before the 'to my <list>' clause, never at the tail).

items.title: Sweep the still-unaudited free-text parsers for phrasing/courtesy/tail leaks
items.why: 90+ parse/detect exports; ~10 verbatim-storing ones swept for courtesy-tail, but parseRemember, parseSaveThatAs, parseWatchThat, parseSaveThat, parseChainSteps, parseRecipeCommand and others handle free text and may leak trailing/labeled phrasing into stored values.
items.how: tsx sandbox probe each with please/thanks/labeled inputs; where a tail or label corrupts the stored value, apply stripTrailingCourtesy (or a labeled-tail strip) + add a test. One parser class per iteration.

items.title: Sweep parsers that take LABELED/multi-clause free text for phrasing leaks beyond courtesy
items.why: Courtesy-tail is now swept across 14 parsers. The residual risk class is LABELED/multi-clause inputs (e.g. 'set my home to <addr>', 'convert 5 usd to eur as of friday', digest/chain step phrasing) where a trailing qualifier or an interior label can corrupt the stored/parsed value in ways a bare courtesy strip won't catch.
items.how: tsx-probe parseSetLocation, parseSavePlace, parseDigestCommand, parseChainSteps, parseFx, parseLogCommand with labeled + qualified inputs; fix leaks with a targeted strip + test. One class per iteration.

items.title: Probe the agent-loop tool DISPATCH + argument extraction, not just the lib parsers
items.why: The lib/*.ts pure parsers are now well-swept. The untested surface is src/agent.ts: how the LLM's tool-call arguments are validated/coerced before dispatch, and whether a malformed/edge arg (empty string, wrong type, huge value, missing required field) produces a wrong reply or throws vs a graceful message. That's where a real texting user's odd phrasing actually lands.
items.how: Read agent.ts dispatch switch; for 3-4 representative tools, feed edge-case args via a mock-LLM tool call and assert a graceful reply (not a throw/blank). Fix any that mishandle. Offline-testable with the injected LLM.

items.title: Probe multi-step agent flows for state bugs across tool calls (session reuse, photo/doc carryover, truncation)
items.why: Single-tool dispatch is now robust. The untested surface is MULTI-call flows: a browse then click then read chain, a screenshot followed by reply (photo carryover), window truncation mid-conversation, session release timing. A state bug here would make the bot lose context or send the wrong artifact.
items.how: Script the mock LLM to emit 3-5 chained tool calls (browse->click->read->reply; screenshot->reply; a long chain that trips truncateWindow) and assert the right backend calls fire in order + the right photo/doc/reply is delivered. Offline via ScriptLLM + recordingBackend.

items.title: Probe handler.ts inbound-message + callback-button flows for state/delivery bugs
items.why: agent.ts core loop is now well-covered. The next untested user-facing surface is src/handler.ts: how an inbound message routes to agent vs a direct parser, how inline-button callbacks (Stop/snooze/gone) mutate state + strip buttons, and whether a photo/doc from the agent is actually forwarded to the channel. A bug here = the user taps a button and nothing happens, or an artifact never sends.
items.how: Read handler.ts dispatch + handleCallback; script inbound texts + callback payloads against a mock channel/backend; assert the right send/editReplyMarkup fires + state changes. Offline via injected deps.

items.title: Apply the same delivery-gating audit to the INBOUND photo/doc + chart/export send sites
items.why: The agent-reply photo/doc path is now gated, but other sendPhoto/sendDocument call sites (inbound photo-to-action res.photo at ~689, chart-it PNG at ~922/1242, csv-export at ~1069) may still write memory as delivered on a failed artifact send - the same class, other entry points.
items.how: Read each sendPhoto/sendDocument site in handler.ts; where a memory write or 'done' state follows an ungated artifact send, gate it on the boolean now returned. Add a test per fixed site.

items.title: Audit PROACTIVE (scheduler/alert/digest) sends for the same artifact/text delivery-gating + a chart in a scheduled digest
items.why: Inbound (user-initiated) delivery is now gated everywhere. The proactive side - schedule-runner/alert-runner/digest firing - sends unprompted; if a scheduled reminder or a digest's chart PNG fails to send, does it mark the task complete/advance anyway (losing that fire), and can a digest even include an artifact? Same reliability class, the side the user CAN'T retry.
items.how: Read schedule-runner.ts/alert-runner.ts/digest send paths; confirm each gates completion/advance on send success (deps.send boolean) incl. any sendPhoto in a digest; add a test for any ungated proactive artifact/text send.

items.title: Audit that every store's failed-write (lastSaveOk=false) is surfaced to the user where it changes what they were told
items.why: Delivery (send) is now gated inbound + proactive. The sibling reliability class is PERSISTENCE: every store exposes lastSaveOk(), but only some callers hedge a failed write to the user (list add, memory). A save that silently fails after a 'saved/added/scheduled' confirmation means the item vanishes on restart while the user was told it stuck - the same trust break, on the disk side.
items.how: grep lastSaveOk() usages + each store mutation caller (contacts, places, recipes, digests, alerts, saved-pages); where a success confirmation follows a mutation whose lastSaveOk isn't checked, hedge the message. One store per iteration; add a test.

items.title: Improve the FIRST-RUN / help / discovery experience (new-user lens, a real product-value move not a bug hunt)
items.why: Reliability + parsing are now deeply swept (delivery + persistence gated, courtesy-tail across 15 parsers, dispatch robust). The higher-value lever that does NOT need Alex is DISCOVERABILITY: a new texter can't tell what Relay does. Audit README/start/help copy + the first-message experience - does the bot surface its best errands (save a page, follow a feed, set a reminder, watch a price, translate, where-to-watch) so a user finds them in the first 10 min?
items.how: Read the /start + /help + empty-message + first-message copy in handler.ts + commands.ts; if the capability surface isn't discoverable, improve the copy/onboarding (a concise 'try these' with real examples grouped by job). Offline-testable: assert the help/start reply names the key tool categories. This is the last high-value NON-owner-gated lever before confirm-to-act / anvil.

items.title: Surface the RIGHT next-capability hint contextually after a relevant answer (not just in /help)
items.why: Onboarding copy covers the cold start, but mid-session discovery is weak: after a user does X, they rarely learn about the adjacent capability (got a price -> could 'watch that'; got a fact -> could 'save that'; asked weather -> could set a morning digest). Some tap-to-act buttons exist (actButtons); audit whether the highest-value adjacencies are actually offered, without nagging.
items.how: Read the post-answer button/nudge logic in handler.ts (canOfferAutomation/actButtons/pickButtons + save-nudge); find a high-value answer type that offers NO next-step hint and add one (gated, once, non-spammy). Offline-testable via the handler harness. If adjacencies are already well-covered, say so + pivot to another lens.

items.title: Next run: either a fresh 3-lens AUDIT (if subagent cap resets in a new session) or surface to Alex that the high-value levers are owner-gated
items.why: After ~10 iterations the autonomously-reachable offline surface (courtesy-tail x15, dispatch, multi-step flows, inbound+proactive delivery gating, persistence hedges, onboarding + mid-session discovery) is deeply swept with 2059 green tests. Continued single-surface probing yields diminishing returns. The two highest-value moves both need Alex (confirm-to-act product-UX decision; start anvil for the overdue live e2e).
items.how: If a NEW session reset the subagent cap, run the real 3-lens parallel AUDIT for a fresh high-value seed. Otherwise do one more targeted inline probe (a surface not yet swept, e.g. voice-message handling, location-share flow, or the compose/draft path) and if it's clean, honestly report to Alex that confirm-to-act + anvil are the only value-adding moves left.

items.title: Surface to Alex: the two remaining high-value levers both need owner action
items.why: After ~11 iterations every autonomously-reachable offline surface is deeply swept (parsing, dispatch, multi-step flows, inbound+proactive delivery gating, persistence hedges across ALL stores, onboarding, mid-session discovery) at 2061 green tests, and the real 3-lens AUDIT is blocked by the exhausted subagent cap (200/200) until a NEW session. Continued inline probing is now genuinely dry.
items.how: OWNER ACTIONS (loop cannot do these): (1) confirm-to-act — decide whether Relay should confirm before a state-changing step + the UX; this is a product decision only Alex can make. (2) start anvil (docker/local) so anvil-live-e2e-when-up can run the overdue real end-to-end errand. (3) OPTIONAL: start a fresh Claude session to reset the subagent cap so the 3-lens parallel AUDIT can seed genuinely new directions. Until one of these, the loop has no value-adding offline move left.

items.title: Find the next genuinely-missing everyday capability (offline/free, like the password tool)
items.why: The password-generator find proves there ARE still real capability gaps (not just bugs) reachable offline. Other common text-a-bot asks may lack a tool: a countdown/stopwatch timer, a tip/split already covered by calculate?, a 'roll a name/lorem/uuid', unit-of-time 'how long until 5pm', a percentage/discount helper, base64/url encode-decode, color hex<->name. Audit the tool set vs common asks + build the highest-value missing one.
items.how: List current TOOLS; brainstorm 8-10 common phone-assistant asks; for each check if a tool/parser handles it (probe); build the highest impact-per-effort genuinely-missing one with a lib+tool+dispatch+prompt+test, same pattern as password. One per iteration.

items.title: Add 'how long until <time today>' countdown (time-of-day, tz-aware) — the one remaining common gap found
items.why: datecalc handles days-until-a-DATE but returns null for 'how long until 5pm' / 'minutes until midnight' — a very common quick ask. It needs the chat's tz (already in profile) + now, then formats h/m remaining. get_time/date_math both miss it.
items.how: Add a parse+compute in datecalc or a small time-until helper: detect 'how long/how many minutes until <clock time>', resolve against the chat's tzOffset + nowMs (both already threaded to the agent env), handle 'tomorrow' rollover when the time already passed today. Wire into date_math or get_time dispatch (they already receive tz+now). Unit-test with injected now/tz. One iteration.

items.title: Final capability-gap scan: check the last few common asks, build if clearly valuable else report vein tapped
items.why: Three capability builds landed (password, encode/decode, time-until). The obvious high-value gaps are now filled. A last scan (UUID/GUID gen, 'roll a random name/lorem', a units-of-DATA convert like MB->GB if not covered, a 'coin flip best of N') confirms whether anything common remains or the vein is tapped and value returns to owner-gated (confirm-to-act, anvil).
items.how: Quick-probe 4-5 remaining candidate asks against the tool set; build the ONE with real user demand + offline feasibility, else honestly report the capability vein is tapped and re-surface the owner levers.

items.title: Capability vein tapped — remaining value is owner-gated (confirm-to-act, anvil live e2e)
items.why: Across ~14 iterations: swept every offline reliability/parsing surface (2100 green) AND shipped 4 new capabilities (password, encode/decode, time-until, data-unit convert). The offline gap-finding vein is now genuinely exhausted - a fresh scan found only low-value candidates. The subagent cap (200/200) blocks the real 3-lens AUDIT until a NEW session.
items.how: OWNER ACTIONS (loop cannot self-serve): (1) confirm-to-act — product-UX decision on whether/how Relay confirms a state-changing step. (2) start anvil (docker/local) for the overdue anvil-live-e2e-when-up real errand. (3) start a FRESH Claude session to reset the subagent cap so the 3-lens AUDIT can seed new directions. Until one of these, further /product-loop runs will find only marginal work.

items.title: Autonomous work exhausted — value is owner-gated (confirm-to-act / anvil / fresh session for AUDIT)
items.why: After ~15 iterations: full offline reliability+parsing sweep AND 5 new capabilities, 2102 green. A fresh capability scan now yields nothing common. Real 3-lens AUDIT still blocked by subagent cap (200/200) until a new session.
items.how: OWNER: (1) decide confirm-to-act (product UX). (2) start anvil for the live e2e. (3) fresh Claude session resets the cap for a real AUDIT. Absent these, /product-loop will only find marginal work — recommend pausing the loop until an owner lever is actioned.

items.title: Probe each existing tool's DOCUMENTED idioms actually work (doc-vs-behavior drift)
items.why: The '% off' bug shows a class: a tool's header/description advertises an idiom that a later refactor broke, and no test covered that exact phrasing. Other tools may have the same doc-vs-behavior drift (worldclock conversions, unit-convert compound forms, datecalc phrasings, translate URL form).
items.how: For each tool, read its doc/description's listed example phrasings + probe them via the lib; where a documented idiom errors or returns null, fix + add a test. One tool per iteration.

items.title: Continue the documented-idiom coverage sweep on the remaining tools (datecalc, translate, directions, scores, flight, feeds)
items.why: The convert_units + calc %-off finds prove doc-vs-behavior drift is a live class. Tools not yet idiom-probed: datecalc (all its listed phrasings), translate (URL/page form), directions (transit/modes), get_scores (team vs league), get_flight (route form), feeds (each follow target type). A documented idiom that errors is a silent dead-end.
items.how: For each remaining tool, extract the example phrasings from its description + doc comment, probe each via the lib/dispatch, fix any that error/return-null-when-they-shouldn't + add a test. One tool per iteration; stop the class when a full pass finds nothing.

items.title: Sweep remaining user-facing MESSAGE surfaces for accuracy (empty-result, rate-limit, cap-hit, ask-clarify copy)
items.why: The friendlyError find shows user-facing message copy is a live probe surface (not just parsing/logic). Other message paths may be vague or wrong: empty-search-result phrasing, per-chat rate-limit message, schedule/list cap-hit copy, the various 'couldn't tell what you meant' clarifiers - do they name the actual problem + a next step?
items.how: Probe each canned user-message path (grep push()/sendMessage string literals + the tool clarify branches); where a message is vague, misleading, or lacks a next step, sharpen it + assert in a test. One surface per iteration.

items.title: Continue probing pure-lib parsers for common phrasings that fall to null (the productive vein)
items.why: Probing individual lib parsers with real user phrasings keeps surfacing genuine dead-ends (calc %-off, convert density, unitprice pack) — a live class distinct from the swept idiom/message veins. Remaining libs to phrase-probe: logs (parseLogCommand/parseLogQuery variants), countdown, geocode/places phrasings, scores team-name forms, qr payload types.
items.how: tsx-probe each remaining lib with 4-5 common real phrasings; where a plausible user phrasing returns null but SHOULD parse, widen the parser + add a test. One lib per iteration; stop when a full pass finds no real dead-end.

items.title: parseLogQuery: handle non-spend COUNT queries ('how much coffee this week', 'how many steps')
items.why: parseLogQuery routes 'how much did I SPEND on X' to a sum + '<tag> trend' to a trend, but a bare 'how much coffee this week' / 'how many beers did I have' (a count sum over a non-money tag) returns null -> the user can log 'log 3 coffees' but can't ask it back naturally.
items.how: Add a count-sum branch: 'how much/many <tag> [window]' (no spend verb) -> { tag, mode:'sum', sinceMs }. Distinguish from the spend-sum path (which tags by the 'on <thing>' object). Widen + test. Keep 'my <tag> trend' as trend.

items.title: Offline veins swept (10 phrasing fixes + 5 capabilities + reliability sweep) — value now owner-gated
items.why: Every autonomously-reachable offline surface is worked out: reliability (delivery+persistence gating), 5 new capabilities, idiom-drift, message-copy, and now the lib-phrasing vein (10 real fixes, several silent-wrong-answer/data-integrity) all at 2114 green. anvil DOWN every run this session; subagent cap 200/200 blocks the real 3-lens AUDIT.
items.how: OWNER: (1) confirm-to-act product-UX decision. (2) start anvil for the overdue live e2e. (3) FRESH Claude session resets the cap for a real 3-lens AUDIT - the highest-leverage move to seed genuinely new directions. Until one, /product-loop returns clean.

items.title: parseSnoozeCommand: support 'snooze X until <day/date>' (date-relative expiry)
items.why: 'snooze btc until monday' / 'until tomorrow' / 'until the 15th' currently fold the clause into the name with no expiry (indefinite). A date-relative snooze is a natural phrasing; reuse parseDate to compute untilMs.
items.how: After the duration match fails, try a 'until <date-phrase>' match; parse the phrase with the existing parseDate (future-preferring) -> untilMs = start-of-that-day. Strip the clause off the name. Reject a past date. +test.

items.title: Probe the other profile/preference setters + capture-reply paths for missed phrasings
items.why: setLocation had 4 missed setter phrasings (just fixed). Sibling setters may too: units preference ('use metric'/'switch to celsius'), the first-run captureLocation reply (parseCityReply - does 'it's Austin'/'Austin' both work?), profile clear. A missed setter on a first-run-critical path silently degrades weather/near-me.
items.how: probe parseCityReply (bare city, 'it's X', 'I'm in X'), any units-preference parse, profileClear phrasings; widen any that miss a natural phrasing + test. One surface per iteration.

items.title: Probe units-preference ('use metric'/'switch to celsius') + profile-clear phrasings
items.why: Location capture is now clean both ways. The sibling profile setters - a units preference ('use metric', 'switch to fahrenheit', 'show me celsius') and profile clear ('forget my location', 'reset my profile') - haven't been phrase-probed; a missed phrasing silently ignores the preference.
items.how: Find where units-pref + profileClear are parsed (profile.ts / handler); probe natural phrasings; widen any that miss + test. Likely the last setter sub-surface.

items.title: parseForgetPlace/parseForgetContact: accept the natural 'forget my gym' / 'forget mom' phrasing
items.why: parseForgetPlace only matches 'forget the gym PLACE' (trailing 'place' required) - 'forget my gym'/'delete my office' return null. parseForgetContact needs "'s contact" or 'contact <name>' - bare 'forget mom' / 'remove mom from contacts' return null. Both are the natural way to delete; a user who saved 'mom' can't easily remove her.
items.how: Widen parseForgetPlace to 'forget/delete/remove (my) <alias>' (guard against a fact/generic forget) + parseForgetContact to 'forget/remove <name>' / 'remove <name> from contacts'. Careful ordering vs parseForgetFact (which also starts 'forget ...'). +tests.

items.title: Wire confirm-to-act: session-persist across turns + flag-gated stash/preview + handler YES/NO
items.why: The tested core (confirm-action.ts) is landed but inert. To make it work end-to-end: (1) the anvil session must survive the preview turn -> the YES turn (currently created+released within one runAgent); (2) the click/type dispatch, when RELAY_CONFIRM_TO_ACT is on + isDangerousAction, must stash a PendingAction + return the preview instead of the flat refuse; (3) the handler must route a YES/NO reply to execute-that-one-click / discard.
items.how: Add a PendingActionStore dep + a keepSession option to runAgent (or a resumable session handle) so the held anvil session persists; gate the click-dispatch branch on confirmToActEnabled(); in handler, before normal routing, if a pending action exists classify the reply (yes->run the exact stashed click in the held session + clear; no/expiry->discard+ack; other->fall through). Real tests with a mock backend asserting the click fires ONLY on yes. Keep default-OFF green.

items.title: confirm-to-act polish: /help mention, telegram inline YES/NO buttons, multi-step act chains
items.why: Core flow ships (text YES/NO, default-OFF). Natural follow-ups now that acting works: (1) document it in /help + README when enabled; (2) on Telegram, offer inline YES/NO buttons (not just text) via the existing callback infra; (3) consider a multi-step act chain (login->add-to-cart->checkout) each gated — but that's a bigger safety surface, owner-gate again. All optional refinements, not blockers.
items.how: Small: add a /help line gated on the flag. Medium: reuse callbacks.ts to attach YES/NO inline buttons to the confirm prompt + route the tap through handleCallback to the same confirmAction. Large/owner-gated: multi-action chains. One per iteration; keep default-OFF.

items.title: Document confirm-to-act in /help + README (gated on the flag being on)
items.why: The feature ships (text + button YES/NO, default-OFF) but is undocumented - an operator who enables RELAY_CONFIRM_TO_ACT + their users won't discover it. A one-line /help mention (only when enabled) + a README note closes the discovery gap.
items.how: In commands.ts HELP, conditionally append a confirm-to-act line when confirmToActEnabled(); add a README bullet under the acting/safety section. Small, default-OFF-safe. Multi-step act chains remain a separate owner-gated item (bigger safety surface).

items.title: calc handles natural phrasing: "20% tip on 47", scientific notation "1e3", factorial "5!"
items.why: Probe found calc("20% tip on 47") errors with "I don’t know tip", "1e3+1" errors on "e", and "5!" errors on "!". A texting user asking "20% tip on 47" gets an error instead of 9.40 (or falls to a slow agent). The tip/split path may be handled elsewhere, but bare calc chokes.
items.how: In calc.ts normalizeExpr: strip/interpret "X% tip on Y" -> Y*X/100 (or route to the tip handler), accept 1e3 scientific-notation number tokens in tokenize, and support trailing ! as factorial. Verify against the existing tip-split path so there’s no double-handling. Add tests.

items.title: Route a bare "how fast is 50 knots" / "50 knots in mph" naturally (no "to")
items.why: Speed conversion now works for "X to Y" / "X in Y", but a natural "how fast is 50 knots" (no explicit target) returns null. A user asking casually gets a slow browse instead of a sensible default (knots->mph, m/s->km/h).
items.how: In parseUnitConvert, when only a source speed unit is given (no "to/in <unit>"), default the target to the user’s locale counterpart (knots/m·s -> mph or km/h). Keep it speed-only so ambiguous single-unit queries elsewhere don’t misfire. Add tests.

items.title: date_math: "how many days until next Friday" / "days until Monday"
items.why: Probe: runDateCalc returns null for "how many days until next Friday" and "days until Monday" — a common casual date question ("how long till the weekend"). Falls to a slow agent turn or an invented answer instead of exact calendar math.
items.how: In datecalc.ts, add a weekday-target branch to the until-parser: resolve "next <weekday>"/"<weekday>" to the next future date matching that weekday (0-6 days out; "next" skips to the following week if today matches). Reuse weekdayName. Add tests for each weekday + "next" semantics.

items.title: date_math: "days since <date>" (elapsed, not remaining)
items.why: Probe: "days since 2020-01-01" returns null — the converse of "days until". Users ask both ("how long since my last...", "days since launch"). Currently only forward countdowns work.
items.how: In datecalc.ts add a "since/ago" branch that computes elapsed days from a past date to today (positive count), mirroring the until-parser. Reject a future date ("since" a future date is nonsense — point them to "until"). Add tests.

items.title: encode_decode: add sha256/md5 hashing + rot13 (common asks beyond base64/hex/url/jwt)
items.why: encoding.ts supports base64/base64url/url/hex/jwt only. "sha256 of hello", "md5 of X", "rot13 this" are common developer/puzzle asks that currently fall to a slow agent turn (or a hallucinated hash — dangerous, since a wrong hash looks right). Node crypto gives exact hashes with no key.
items.how: Add codecs sha256/sha1/md5 (encode-only, via node:crypto createHash) + rot13 (encode=decode, pure) to EncOp + parseEncodingRequest keyword matching + runEncoding. Guard: hashing is one-way, so "decode sha256" -> friendly refusal. Tests for each. Update the tool description.

items.title: encode_decode: text<->binary + text<->decimal codepoints
items.why: "binary of A", "hello in binary", "decode this binary 01001000..." is a common learning/puzzle ask with no home — falls to a slow browse. Deterministic + keyless.
items.how: Add a binary codec (encode: each char -> 8-bit; decode: 8-bit groups -> chars) to encoding.ts, mirroring hex. Tolerate spaces between bytes on decode. Tests + tool-description mention.

Bare verbs + question words removed; kept explicit lookup/data phrases (check the/look up/search for/weather/the price/the score/summarize/whats the...). "remind me to find my keys / water the plants / top up my card" now correctly echo. 864 tests green.

forget-fact now matches whole words, not raw substrings — "forget that I drink tea" no longer silently deletes "my niece Teagan birthday". matchScore tiers (exact=3 / all-words=2 / some-words=1) delete only the BEST tier; forget returns the removed facts text; the confirm now LISTS exactly what was forgotten so a mismatch is visible + correctable. 866 tests green.

At the 30-fact memory cap, adding a new fact used to silently drop the oldest (often the most important). add() now returns the evicted fact text + a dup flag; the remember confirm warns and NAMES what aged out ("I was at my memory limit, so I let go of: ..."). 868 tests green.

First location-dependent errand (weather/near me/directions) with no saved city now asks once, stashes the errand, saves the reply (+infers tz and re-stamps recurring reminders), then re-runs the errand — instead of the agent asking the city every time and leaving tz unset. needsLocationContext + parseCityReply in profile.ts; pendingLocation map + hasLocation/captureLocation deps; a non-city reply bails out cleanly. 876 tests green.

A large "get back to me" errand (dispatch phrasing, or a scale cue + length) is now ACKed instantly ("on it — I will text you when done") and run DETACHED off the per-chat chain with a raised step budget (BACKGROUND_MAX_STEPS=20, agent maxSteps clamped to 30 ceiling), delivered unprompted + cached for more/link. Failures still notify (no black hole). isBackgroundErrand/stripDispatchPhrasing in lib/background.ts; enableBackgroundErrands dep (RELAY_BACKGROUND_ERRANDS, on by default). Instinct dispatch-and-ping parity, read-only. 888 tests green.

Added a searchable per-chat log of PAST answers Relay gave (AnswerLog, capped 100, oldest-drop). "what was that sushi place you found?" / "resend the flights" now searches by keyword + replies from the log, no agent re-run. Clean synchronous + background answers are logged (degraded/binaries skipped). isAnswerRecall/recallKeywords in lib/answer-log.js; recallAnswers/logAnswer deps; RELAY_ANSWERS_FILE. Distinct from notes recall (answers GIVEN vs facts stored). 898 tests green.

Fixed 3 regressions in the just-shipped background-errand path (found by the refill audit): (1) result now written to conversation memory so a follow-up has context; (2) delivery writes the PING sub-slot instead of clobbering the inbound answer paging (same class as proactive-clobbers-drilldown-cache); (3) cap 2 concurrent detached runs per chat, over-cap runs synchronously (no browser-pool starvation). Plus recall-staleness-label: recalled answers now show a relativeAge + a >6h refresh nudge. 903 tests green.

A bare city now sets the right reminder timezone without the user typing UTC-5 — closes the wrong-hour reminder bug at its root. inferTzFromLocation maps ~150 common cities / US state abbrevs / countries to a standard (non-DST) offset; parseSetLocation + parseCityReply infer tz from the city when no explicit UTC given (explicit still wins, unknown city -> no guess). 907 tests green.

A watch can now DO, not just notify: add "then run <recipe>" and when the alert fires Relay runs that saved recipe (current task resolved at fire time) and appends its result to the ping. Alert.then + parse of the trailing then-clause (stripped before trigger parsing) + withThen helper at all 3 notify sites (predicate/threshold/feed) + runThen dep wired to the recipe store; stays read-only. Confirm + /alerts surface it. Gone/failed recipe leaves the base alert intact. 914 tests green.

Numeric watches now accumulate a time series: each check with an extractable value appends {t,v} (capped 400, oldest-drop). "how has btc moved this week" / "btc trend" answers from stored points — first->last + delta + %, high/low, span — NO agent/LLM/re-fetch. Alert.series + recordPoint/seriesOf on the store; parseTrendRequest + summarizeSeries (pure); recordPoint wired in the runner (numeric non-feed checks); watchTrend handler branch before answer-recall. 923 tests green.

A paywalled article link (NYT/WSJ/Medium etc.) that renders a subscribe/register STUB (short body, not the empty-shell case) is now flagged to the agent instead of summarized as if it were the article — the marker tells it to say the page is paywalled + offer a free source (web_search the headline). formatPageForModel gained a looksPaywalled check gated on a short body (<1500 non-ws) so a long article mentioning subscribe in a footer still passes through. 927 tests green.

Background errands now survive a restart. A dispatched errand is recorded in a persistent BackgroundStore (id+chatId+original text) + cleared when it settles; on startup the worker drains the store and, per planErrandReplay, RE-RUNS fresh errands (re-injects the original message) or sends an honest "I was interrupted" note for stale ones (>6h). No more silently-dropped "I will text you when done" promise. bgErrandAdd/Done handler deps; RELAY_BACKGROUND_FILE. 933 tests green.

Hardened the crash-recovery shipped last iteration (audit found 3 defects): replay now runs under the errand EXISTING id via a shared dispatchBackground + handle.resumeErrand — no drain-gap data loss, no second ACK; the store keeps the record (list+reinstate bumps attempts in place, no drain) so a poison task that crashes each boot is dropped after MAX_ERRAND_ATTEMPTS(3) instead of crash-looping + re-spamming. 935 tests green.

web_search no longer a single point of failure: Bing stays primary, but on an empty result (bot-check / markup change) it now falls back to DuckDuckGo no-JS HTML endpoint (html.duckduckgo.com/html/). Refactored into searchBing/searchDuck + shared collectResults; unwrapDuckUrl recovers the //duckduckgo.com/l/?uddg= redirect target. Each provider its own session, deduped+SSRF-filtered. 938 tests green.

Track N items as ONE watch: "watch markets: btc price; eth price; gold price" (semicolon-separated) creates a watchlist whose members each carry their own last value; a check runs them all and sends ONE grouped ping of only the members that CHANGED. First run seeds silently; per-member advances deferred to the post-send commit. Alert.members + memberLabel + setMemberLasts store method; checkAlert watchlist branch (parallel member runs, changed-only lines); /alerts + confirm surface it. 946 tests green.

An over-cap "once" reminder was deferred with no age limit, so a chat with many recurring watches (always over the hourly proactive cap) could starve an explicit promise ("meds at 3pm") past its time forever. Now once it is overdue by more than a grace window (RELAY_ONCE_CAP_GRACE_MS, default 15min) it is delivered ANYWAY — an explicit single promise outweighs anti-spam. Under the window it still defers for a free slot. 947 tests green.

A compare with a file cue ("as a CSV"/spreadsheet/export/download) now attaches a proper CSV document (via the existing sendDocument path) instead of pasting a truncated JSON blob — keepable, sortable, shareable. New rowsToCsv (RFC-4180 escaping, union header); agent threads doc+docName so a CSV is named comparison.csv not page.pdf; gated on a CSV_REQUEST_RE cue so a plain compare is unchanged. 954 tests green.

Added a convert_currency tool backed by a keyless FX API (open.er-api.com) — "200 USD in EUR" is now instant + exact instead of a slow scrape. New src/lib/fx.ts (normalizeCurrency incl symbols/words, fxUrl, parseFxRate, convertCurrency with injected fetch) + backend.convertCurrency + agent tool/dispatch/prompt. Live-verified the API (result:success, real USD->EUR/GBP rates). 964 tests green.

A shared Telegram location pin (attach->Location, the natural "near me" move) was text-less + silently dropped. Now parseUpdates maps it to an InboundMessage with coords; the handler saves them to the profile (lat/lng, surfaced in the agent context line for near-me/directions) + acks, or runs the caption as a task if one was sent. hasLocation counts coords too. 968 tests green.

Fixed 2 defects the refill audit found: (1) watchlist member checks ran an unbounded Promise.all over up to 8 members, bypassing the anvil-pool bound (browser-pool exhaustion; degraded members silently dropped) — now mapPool at WATCHLIST_CONCURRENCY(3); (2) CSV export did not guard formula injection — csvCell now prefixes =/+/-/@ cells with a quote so a scraped =HYPERLINK/=cmd cell is inert in Excel/Sheets. 969 tests green.

Added a get_weather tool (the #1 first errand had no backend — the agent guessed a forecast URL or scraped a JS shell). Keyless Open-Meteo: geocode city->coords then current+today forecast. New src/lib/weather.ts (weatherDesc/parseGeocode/parseForecast/formatWeather/getWeather with injected fetch) + backend.getWeather + agent tool/dispatch/prompt; honors the chat saved coords (near-me weather with no place) + unit preference. Live-verified the APIs (Austin geocode + real forecast). Directions/near-me-POI still seeded for later. 982 tests green.

A shared location pin used to send ~1m coords to the LLM on EVERY later message forever + near-me resolved against a stale spot. Coords now carry coordsAt + expire after COORDS_TTL_MS (RELAY_COORDS_TTL_MS, default 6h): profiles.freshCoords + contextLine(now) omit expired coords, so a one-time pin informs only near-term near-me/weather then stops leaking. Home location stays durable. All coord-reading sites (profileContext, weatherCoords, hasLocation, proactive contextFor) now freshness-gated. 983 tests green.

convert_currency no longer claims a money figure is "live" (the source refreshes ~daily): parseFx now returns the API time_last_update_utc as a YYYY-MM-DD asOf, formatConversion appends "as of <date>" + the prompt says report it. Also fmtRate renders a tiny inverse rate at adaptive precision (IDR->USD 0.0000238, not "0.0000"). parseFxRate kept as a back-compat shim. 987 tests green.

Added a compose tool — the non-gated slice of Instinct acting: the agent drafts an email/text and returns a copy block + a one-tap mailto:/sms: deep link the USER sends; Relay never sends (safety guard untouched). New src/lib/compose.ts (mailtoLink/smsLink RFC-encoded, formatDraft) + agent tool/dispatch/prompt; passed to the user verbatim. Closes the read-only "here is what I found" dead-end. 995 tests green.

Watchlist members whose 4-word label collides (e.g. "news on tesla model 3" / "...model y" both -> "news on tesla model") now get a numeric suffix so labels are unique. setMemberLasts keys on label, so a collision used to update the wrong member + one re-fired every check. 996 tests green.

Fixed the CSV formula-injection guard (shipped 2 iters ago) that also quoted legitimate negative numbers (-5.2 -> '-5.2), breaking sort/sum in the exported sheet. Now a plain numeric cell is left untouched; a non-numeric =/+/-/@ lead is still guarded. Also flipped watchlist-member-label-collision this iteration. 997 tests green.

Added a find_nearby tool — "coffee near me"/"nearest pharmacy" (advertised but unbuilt) now returns real nearby places via keyless OSM: Nominatim geocodes a named area, Overpass around:<coords> returns POIs by category with distance + opening_hours + phone. New src/lib/places.ts (categoryFilters, haversineKm, overpassQuery, parseNominatim, parsePlaces, formatPlaces, findNearby w/ injected GET+POST fetch) + backend.findNearby + agent tool/dispatch/prompt; uses saved coords for near-me, honors unit pref (mi/km). Live-verified Nominatim+Overpass. 1012 tests green.

Added a directions tool — "how far is the airport"/"directions to X" (advertised but unbuilt) now returns distance + travel time via keyless OSM: Nominatim geocodes both endpoints, OSRM public server routes them (driving/walking/cycling inferred from phrasing). New src/lib/directions.ts (osrmUrl lng,lat order, routeMode, parseOsrm, formatRoute, getDirections w/ injected fetch, reuses places nominatim) + backend.getDirections + agent tool/dispatch/prompt; from = user coords when omitted, honors unit pref (mi/km). Live-verified OSRM (Austin downtown->airport 18.2km/22min). 1024 tests green.

Added a calendar_event tool — an event/deadline now ends in the user calendar instead of dead-ending at text. Emits a Google Calendar template link + an .ics VEVENT as a data: URL (all-day date or timed UTC). New src/lib/calendar.ts (buildIcs RFC-5545-escaped, gcalLink, formatCalendar) + agent tool/dispatch/prompt; pure formatting, never touches the send/pay guard (user taps to add). 1032 tests green.

applySlots no longer stuffs one arg into every slot: a recipe with DISTINCT slots ("track {item} at {store}") now fills by name=value pairs (item=milk store=HEB, quotes supported) or by position (comma then whitespace); single-slot + repeated-same-name behavior unchanged (back-compat). New slotNames helper. Makes parameterized recipes actually reusable. Help updated. 1037 tests green.

get_weather no longer always returns the biggest same-name city: geocode now fetches 5 candidates (parseGeocodeAll) and pickCandidate prefers the one within ~250km of the user saved coords, else the top match. Agent passes weatherCoords as near when a place is named. So "weather in Portland" for a Boston user resolves to Portland ME, not OR. parseGeocode kept as a back-compat shim. 1043 tests green.

compose no longer echoes a malformed recipient as "To: john at x.com" while the deep link is blank-addressed (misleads the user into thinking it is addressed). formatDraft now shows the To: line only when the recipient is VALID for the kind (email/phone), else a "Couldn t parse ... add the recipient yourself" note. 1044 tests green.

Fixed a crash the refill audit found in the just-shipped calendar_event: it was the only tool handler with no try/catch, and gcalLink threw RangeError on a non-ISO startDate -> escaped runAgent + killed the whole turn (an unpadded date also produced a silently-broken .ics). normalizeIsoDate (strict + round-trip) now gates buildIcs/gcalLink so a bad date is dropped, and the dispatch is wrapped. 1047 tests green.

Propagated the weather region-disambiguation to find_nearby + directions: Nominatim now fetches 5 candidates (parseNominatimAll) and pickNominatim(bias) prefers the one within ~250km of a hint. directions biases the origin geocode to the user coords + the DESTINATION geocode to the origin, so "directions to Springfield" from Boston resolves to Springfield MA not IL. find_nearby biases a named area to the user coords. bias is a hint that never overrides an explicit from/coords. parseNominatim kept as a back-compat shim. 1052 tests green.

find_nearby now expands its search radius 3->10->30km until results appear, so "nearest ER/hospital" is no longer a dangerous false-negative just past 3km; it also distinguishes a failed area geocode (area_not_found) from a genuinely-empty result, and surfaces the radius when it widened past 3km. findNearby returns a NearbyOutcome ({places,radiusKm} | {error}); agent dispatch handles each case. 1054 tests green.

Recipes can now be multi-step workflows: a task with >>-separated steps runs each in order, feeding the PRIOR step output into the next as context ("cheapest flight to {city} >> weather + news there >> summarize"). An "if <kw>: <step>" gate stops the chain when the prior output lacks the keyword; a degraded/empty step also stops it. New parseChainSteps/isChain in recipes.ts + src/chain-runner.ts (runChain, injected agent, read-only — safety intact); handler routes a chained /run through runChainRecipe (rate-limited, cached for drilldown). 1064 tests green.

Added /templates — a cold user browses a curated catalog (morning briefing chain, price watch, top news, HN, job watch, commute) and installs one in a tap (/templates morning), seeding the first saved recipe so the recipe/digest/schedule retention flywheel actually starts. Static TEMPLATES + getTemplate/templateCatalog in lib/templates.ts; handler /templates branch installs via recipeSaveNamed; added to KNOWN_COMMANDS + the Telegram menu + help. 1071 tests green.

Routed the geo/transcript/fetch_json default fetch helpers (defaultFetchText/defaultFetchTextPost/defaultFetchJson) through safeFetch (redirect:manual + isUrlSafe per hop) instead of a raw redirect:follow, matching scrape s SSRF discipline — a 3xx to an internal host is now re-validated on every hop. Consistency hardening; safeFetch already unit-tested. 1071 tests green.

Fixed 3 defects the refill audit found in just-shipped recipe-chaining: (1) a scheduled chained recipe ran the literal "a >> b" as one agent task — added a runChain dep to the schedule runner so it fires as a workflow; (2) no step cap -> MAX_CHAIN_STEPS=6 in parseChainSteps; (3) if-gate matched "in stock" inside "out of stock" -> containsUnnegated negation guard. 1075 tests green.

A brand-new user's first "remind me at 7am" no longer misfires at UTC then hands them offset math. Added a scheduleNeedsTz dep (index.ts reuses the isClockTime/no-tz predicate WITHOUT scheduling); handler intercepts a clock-time reminder from a tz-less chat BEFORE scheduleAdd, stashes msg.text in pendingLocation, asks the city once; the existing city-capture path infers tz (inferTzFromLocation) + re-runs the stashed schedule, now firing at the right local hour. Falls through untouched when a tz is already known or capture isn't wired. 3 handler tests (asks+stashes / city reply re-runs / tz-set schedules directly). 1078 tests green.

Fixed 2 chain defects. (1) A stopped-early chain (if-gate failed or a step degraded) returned an INTERMEDIATE step's output as if it were the complete answer — runChainRecipe now returns {final, stoppedEarly, stepsDone, stepsTotal} and the handler prefixes a '⚠️ Couldn't finish all the steps (N of M)' note instead of passing the partial off as done; legacy bare-string return still accepted. (2) A long chain held the per-chat lock with no 'still working' ping (read as a hang) — armed the same one-shot progress timer the agent path uses on the chain branch. 3 handler tests (partial flagged / full sends clean / progress armed). 1081 tests green.

Added a get_quote agent tool so 'what's Tesla at?' / 'AAPL price' answers instantly instead of degrading to a slow, flaky web_search+scrape (currency already had a fast tool; stocks didn't). New src/lib/quote.ts hits the keyless Yahoo Finance chart JSON (no signup) via the injected safeFetch-backed fetchText; returns price + currency ($/£/etc) + a ▲/▼ day-change% + as-of UTC time. Handles bare US tickers, dotted foreign listings (VOD.L, SHOP.TO), and indices (^GSPC); unknown symbol -> null -> the tool tells the agent to fall back to web_search. Wired into the BrowserBackend interface + defaultBackend + SYSTEM_PROMPT + tool surface.
