WIRED confirm-to-act end-to-end (default-OFF opt-in, owner-approved). agent.ts: tracks lastUrl on browse; on a dangerous CLICK with RELAY_CONFIRM_TO_ACT on + a live session, stashes {selector,label,url}, returns a formatConfirmPrompt reply + pendingAction (instead of the flat refuse). handler.ts: stashes pendingAction post-run; a whole-message YES on the next turn runs deps.confirmAction (fresh anvil session: navigate->click->release) + acks '✅ Done', NO discards, TTL-expiry drops, anything-else falls through. index.ts: confirmAction dep wired ONLY when the flag is on (else undefined -> flow inert, agent hard-refuses as before). +4 handler tests (yes-runs/no-discards/other-falls-through/inert-when-unwired) + LIVE-verified the execute path (flag on, real anvil navigate+click OK). 2149 green. call-tested: true. Default-OFF = byte-identical behavior; the read-only boundary is unchanged unless an operator opts in. This closes the acting-gap: Relay can now DO (Instinct's core), under explicit per-action consent, without abandoning safety.

Added Telegram inline YES/NO buttons to the confirm-to-act prompt (reusing callbacks.ts): new 'confirm' callback kind (bare cy/cn opcodes, round-trip) + confirmButtons() (✅ Yes / ✋ No row); handler attaches them to the preview (highest-priority keyboard, overrides pick/act CTAs) + a confirm-tap in handleCallback runs the SAME stashed-click logic as the text gate (yes->confirmAction, no->discard, expired/consumed->honest note, editReplyMarkup retires buttons so a re-tap can't double-fire). Text YES/NO still works for a buttonless channel (console). +5 tests. 2154 green. Default-OFF unchanged (confirmButtons only render when a pendingAction exists, which only happens when the flag's on).

/help + README now mention approve-to-act — but ONLY when RELAY_CONFIRM_TO_ACT is on (line appended to HELP at call time so the env flag reads live; absent by default). Closes the discovery gap: an operator who enables the feature now has their users learn it exists + how to approve (tap ✅ Yes / reply yes; no/timeout discards). README gained a default-OFF opt-in paragraph under the safety section. +1 test (asserts absent-by-default, present-when-on, both /help and bare help). 2155 green.

Added a SPEED dimension to the unit converter (base m/s): mph, km/h (+kph/kmh/kmph/"km per hour"), m/s, ft/s, knots (kn/kt). normalizeUnit now canonicalizes the slashed + spoken forms ("km per hour"->km/h, "miles per hour"->mph, "feet per second"->ft/s) and the parser char-class allows "/" so a speed unit is captured whole. "100 km/h to mph"->62.14, "60 mph"->96.56 km/h, "60 mph"->88 ft/s, "50 knots"->57.54 mph — all exact; cross-dim (speed->length) still null. Tool description + SYSTEM_PROMPT + /help updated so the LLM routes speed queries here (not web_search). +4 tests, 2159 green. Fixes a daily travel errand that used to fall to a slow agent browse.

calc.ts now handles 3 natural phrasings that used to ERROR: (1) "20% tip on 47" / "18% gratuity on 200" -> the tip AMOUNT (Y*X/100 = 9.40), matching the SYSTEM_PROMPT example (was "I dont know tip"); (2) scientific notation "1e3"/"6.02e23"/"2.5e-4" as a number (was unknown "e"; bare "e" still errors since no digits follow); (3) trailing factorial "5!"->120 with whole-number + 170-overflow guards (was "Unexpected character !"). Existing percent/mod/currency idioms unchanged. +4 tests, 2163 green.

A bare speed query with no explicit target now defaults to the sensible counterpart (convert-speed-bare-query): "how fast is 50 knots"/"50 knots"->57.54 mph, "100 km/h"->62.14 mph, "60 mph"->96.56 km/h, "30 m/s"->108 km/h. Added a no-target fallback in parseUnitConvert GATED to speed units only, so a bare "5 kg"/"10 miles"/"3 apples" still returns null (not force-converted) and unrelated messages fall through to the agent. +2 tests, 2165 green.

"how many days until next Friday" / "days until Monday" / "how long until sunday" now resolve to the next matching weekday (date-until-weekday) instead of null. parseDate gained a weekday-target branch (full names + abbrevs sun/mon/tue/wed/thu/fri/sat, optional next/this/coming) -> nearest FUTURE date (a bare weekday on its own day = next week, never today). Gated to real weekday words so "may"/"launch"/junk still return null. +2 tests, 2167 green. Fills a common casual date question that fell to a slow browse.

"days since <date>" / "how long since July 4" / "weeks since 2026-08-01" now give elapsed days (the converse of "until"), was null. runDateCalc gained a since/after branch computing today-target; a FUTURE date honestly redirects ("still N days away — ask days until") rather than a negative count; reuses parseTrailingDate so "days since my anniversary on 1990-05-06" works. +1 test, 2168 green.

encode_decode gained sha256/sha1/md5 hashing (node:crypto, exact hex digests — a hallucinated hash LOOKS right but is wrong, a real trust risk) + rot13 (its own inverse). Parser matches "sha256 of X", "md5 hash of Y", "rot13 ..."; hashing is one-way so "reverse/decode this sha256" gets a friendly refusal, not a fake answer. Verified vs known vectors (sha256(hello), md5(hello), sha1(abc)). Tool description + /help updated. +5 tests, 2173 green.
